title: Sustainability Executive
description:
Job Overview

Over the years, Hong Leong Asia (HLA) has grown into an established Asian multinational with operations across Singapore, Malaysia and China. Building upon deep expertise in the manufacture of building materials and powertrain solutions, HLA works closely with customers across Asia and beyond to advance innovative urban solutions for a more sustainable world. This role is responsible for supporting the Group with the sustainability reporting process of Hong Leong Asia Ltd and Hong Leong Global Enterprise which covers ESG data collection and management, data verification, internal controls and performance monitoring.

Key Responsibilities

1. Sustainability Reporting & ESG Data Management

Support the preparation of the Group's annual Sustainability Report and sustainability disclosures in accordance with applicable reporting requirements and frameworks, including SGX sustainability reporting requirements, GRI Standards and other relevant sustainability disclosure standards.

Coordinate with reporting business units across Singapore, Malaysia and China to collect sustainability and ESG data, supporting information and explanations required for Group reporting.

Compile, consolidate and maintain ESG datasets covering areas including energy, fuel consumption, carbon emissions, waste and circularity, health and safety, people and community as well as supply chain indicators.

Review submitted data for completeness, consistency and reasonableness, and follow up with business units to resolve discrepancies or unusual trends.

Maintain sustainability reporting workbooks, data repositories, supporting documentation and reporting records to strengthen data integrity and auditability.

Gradually develop the capability to independently coordinate the annual sustainability reporting cycle and support the future transition to digitised reporting.

2. Data Verification, Controls & Assurance

Conduct sample verification of ESG data against source documents and supporting records to ensure accuracy and completeness.

Assist in strengthening internal ESG data collection processes, definitions, controls and documentation across reporting business units.

Maintain appropriate audit trails and supporting documentation in preparation for internal review and external assurance.

Support external assurance exercises and respond to information requests from auditors, consultants and other relevant parties.

Identify recurring data gaps and recommend improvements to reporting processes and controls.

3. Sustainability Performance Monitoring

Maintain database of progress against the Group's sustainability targets and key performance indicators.

Assist in preparing quarterly sustainability performance reports and dashboards for Management and the Board Sustainability Committee and/or Board-level reporting.

Analyse ESG performance trends and highlight significant movements, gaps or areas requiring further explanation from business units.

Support the development of clearer performance indicators and reporting dashboards to improve management visibility of sustainability performance.

Skills Required

Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and comfortable working with large datasets from multiple business units.

Strong attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies or gaps in quantitative and qualitative information.

Good analytical, organisational and coordination skills.

Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to follow up effectively with stakeholders across different functions, culture and geographies.

Familiarity with GRI Standards, SGX sustainability reporting requirements and/or ISSB standards would be advantageous.

Exposure to carbon accounting, environmental data, sustainability assurance or ESG reporting systems would be an advantage.

Willingness to learn the operational and technical aspects of the Group's businesses and develop progressively into an independent sustainability reporting role.

Qualifications and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Sustainability, Environmental Studies, Business, Finance, Accounting, Engineering or a related discipline.

Minimum 1–2 years of relevant working experience in sustainability, ESG reporting, corporate reporting, environmental management, data analysis or related fields.

Exposure to sustainability reporting frameworks and governance processes.

Over the years, Hong Leong Asia has grown into an established Asian multinational known for our market leadership and financial strength. Having built core expertise in the manufacturing of building materials and diesel engines, we work closely with our customers across the rapidly urbanizing Asia to develop and deliver innovative solutions that will improve quality of life and drive sustainability for cities of the future.

We pride ourselves on making HLA a harmonious place to work at and to develop your long-term career. Our employees’ growth and well-being are of utmost priority to us, therefore we strive to offer opportunities, support and rewards for personal and professional growth. We are looking for inspiring, talented individuals to be part of the HLA family and help drive our vision and sustainability agenda.

title: Regional Operations Director
description:
JLL supports the Whole You, personally and professionally.

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology to our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people in our industry; and we support them through professional growth, flexibility, and personalized benefits to manage life in and outside of work. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades, and technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, we empower you to shape a brighter way forward so you can thrive professionally and personally.

Regional Operations Director

Job Summary/Goals
Lead integrated facilities management operations across the APAC (including GC exc. West Asia) portfolio for a major multi-service corporate client, ensuring operational excellence, financial performance, risk compliance, and exceptional employee experience delivery across a portfolio exceeding 1.5 million square feet.

As the primary regional operational lead across 10+ countries, the role partners closely with the Regional Account Executive and cross-functional service line leaders to deliver contractual commitments, operational transformation, technology-enabled improvements, and strategic business outcomes while leading a regional team of 80 employees. The role reports to Regional Account Executive.

What Your Day-to-Day Will Look Like
• Own the operational heartbeat of the account: You'll oversee integrated FM service delivery across 1.5M+ sq. ft. spanning 10+ countries in APAC (including GC exc. West Asia), ensuring KPIs, Joint Business Plans, and compliance targets are consistently met.
• Be the trusted partner to senior client stakeholders: From day-to-day engagement to executive business reviews, you'll act as a strategic advisor, communicating performance, managing risks, and strengthening client partnership at every level.
• Lead and develop a regional team of 80: You'll coach, develop, and inspire a geographically dispersed, multicultural team, building capability, managing succession, and creating a high-performance culture across borders.
• Drive digital transformation and innovation: You'll champion the adoption of AI tools, smart building technologies, automation, and data analytics, leading change management to embed new ways of working across teams and vendors.
• Manage financial and commercial performance: From budgeting and forecasting to vendor governance and supply chain spending, you'll support financial targets and identify savings opportunities that deliver value for the client.
• Lead on risk, compliance, and governance: You'll own Health & Safety, engineering risk programmes, audit readiness, and incident reporting — fostering a risk-aware culture across all sites and service lines.
• Shape and execute the regional strategy: Working closely with the Regional Account Executive, you'll translate client priorities into operational action, driving consistency, best practice, and continuous improvement across the entire APAC (including GC exc. West Asia).

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Client & Operational Leadership
• Partner with the Regional Account Executive to maintain strong engagement with client stakeholders and ensure alignment between operational delivery and client business priorities.
• Lead the execution of the regional operational strategy and service delivery across the APAC (including GC exc. West Asia) portfolio.
• Drive a culture of service excellence, continuous improvement, and accountability across all sites and teams.
• Ensure delivery of contractual obligations, including achievement of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), Joint Business Plan priorities, and Partnership Incentive Fund (PIF) objectives.
• Partner with Workplace Experience, Projects, Real Estate, Engineering, Risk, and other service line teams to ensure integrated and seamless service delivery.
• Oversee operational governance, reporting, systems, and data integrity to ensure compliance, consistency, and effective decision-making across the portfolio.
• Partner with Workplace Experience, Projects, Engineering, Real Estate, Risk & Compliance, and other service lines to deliver integrated workplace solutions and positive employee experience outcomes.
• Monitor Planned Preventive Maintenance (PPM) programs to ensure compliance with local regulations, client standards, and JLL operational requirements.
• Ensuring robust business continuity, crisis management, and emergency response procedures are implemented, maintained, and regularly communicated across all sites.
• Accountable for the regional success of the "autonomous operations" model (EPIC), including delivery, performance, and outcomes.

Digital and Innovation Leadership
• Drive operational innovation and digital transformation initiatives across the portfolio, leveraging technology, automation, AI-enabled tools, smart building solutions, and data-driven insights to improve operational efficiency, service quality, scalability, reporting, and employee experience.
• Partner with account leadership, technology teams, and service line leaders to strengthen digital adoption, operational analytics, and technology-enabled decision-making across the portfolio.
• Lead adoption and change management initiatives related to operational technologies, digital workflows, analytics platforms, and AI-enabled capabilities across regional teams and vendors.

Financial & Commercial Management
• Support the Regional Account Executive in achieving financial targets, operational efficiencies, savings initiatives, and commercial objectives across the portfolio.
• Oversee regional budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and operational expenditure management.
• Provide governance oversight of vendor performance, supply chain expenditure, and commercial compliance activities, including contract changes and service performance management.
People Leadership & Talent Development
• Lead, Inspire and develop a regional team of 80 employees across geographically dispersed and multicultural sites, fostering a high-performance, inclusive, and accountable culture.
• Directly manage the professional development of all direct reports, providing regular coaching, feedback and career growth opportunities aligned to JLL’s talent framework. Ensure team members have clear objectives, professional development plans and participate in training and continuous learning activities.
• Prepare and maintain a robust Succession Plan for the account, identifying and developing high-potential talent to ensure business continuity and pipeline readiness in partnership with HR.
• Champion employee engagement and wellbeing across the regional team, modelling JLL behaviours for the team.
• Manage team resourcing and workload allocation to support effective and sustainable operations.
• Participate in remuneration and talent review processes as required.

Risk, Compliance & Governance
• Promote a strong risk-aware culture across the account and ensure compliance with client, local regulatory, and JLL Health, Safety, Environment, and Risk Management standards.
• Be accountable for regional Health & Safety and Engineering/Design/Risk program and its deliverables.
• Ensure all incidents are reported and managed in accordance with client and JLL procedures.
• Oversee operational risk mitigation activities and ensure appropriate escalation processes are in place across the region.
• Support audit readiness and ensure operational compliance documentation is maintained and accessible.
• Partner with internal risk, compliance, and safety teams to continuously strengthen governance standards and operational resilience.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management
• Act as a trusted advisor and operational partner to senior client stakeholders and internal leadership teams.
• Promote open, constructive, and collaborative relationships across client teams, JLL functions, and external vendors.
• Communicate operational priorities, performance outcomes, risks, and improvement initiatives clearly and effectively.
• Lead by example in demonstrating JLL values, ethical standards, professionalism, and inclusive leadership behaviours.
• Drive operational transformation and innovation initiatives that improve workplace experience, sustainability outcomes, and service efficiency across the portfolio.

Key Performance Measures
Performance will be measured through achievement of:
• Contractual KPIs
• Client satisfaction and employee experience outcomes
• Financial performance, budget management, and savings targets
• Operational consistency and service quality
• Compliance, audit, and safety performance
• Adoption and successful implementation of operational technology and innovation initiatives
• Improvement in operational efficiency, automation, reporting quality, or digital maturity outcomes
• Sustainability and operational efficiency objectives
• Timely and accurate operational and financial reporting
• Team engagement, capability development, and retention

Key Stakeholders
• Regional Account Executive
• Client Regional Leadership and Governance Teams
• Country internal Workplace Experience Teams and client-side leadership
• Engineering Operations and EOS Teams
• Projects and Real Estate Teams
• Finance, Procurement, HR, and Risk Functions
• External Vendors and Service Providers

Skills & Experience
• Strong leadership capability with experience managing geographically dispersed and multicultural teams across APAC & Greater China.
• Strong operational, commercial, and financial management skills.
• Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and clients.
• Experience leading or supporting digital transformation, operational technology adoption, automation initiatives, or data-driven operational improvement programs within facilities management, workplace operations, or corporate real estate environments.
• Demonstrated ability to leverage data, analytics, and technology insights to support operational decision-making, performance optimization, and continuous improvement.
• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving capability.
• Strong communication and presentation skills, with fluency in English required.
• Additional APAC regional language capability is advantageous.
• Demonstrated ability to lead change, continuous improvement, and operational transformation initiatives.
• Resilient and adaptable in fast-paced and evolving operational environments.
• Strong digital, systems, and data literacy, including workplace technologies, operational reporting platforms, and analytics tools.
• Ability to balance strategic priorities with operational execution.

Competencies
• Leadership: Sets clear objectives and measurable outcomes for teams and stakeholders. Motivates and develops teams to achieve operational excellence and client outcomes. Demonstrates ethical leadership and accountability consistent with JLL values and standards.
• Decision Making: Applies sound judgment and data-driven thinking to resolve complex operational and commercial challenges.
•Communication: Builds trusted relationships and communicates effectively with stakeholders across all organizational levels.
• Strategic Thinking: Leverages data, technology, and commercial insight to improve operational outcomes and support transformation initiatives.

Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related discipline preferred.
• 10+ years of progressive experience in facilities management, workplace operations, property management, or integrated facilities services.
• Experience leading operational transformation initiatives involving workplace technology, automation, smart building systems, AI-enabled solutions, or digital FM platforms preferred.
• Experience leading and working as part of complex, multi-country multi-service corporate accounts across APAC & Greater China.
• Experience managing large-scale operational teams, vendors, and client stakeholder relationships in a regional environment preferred.
If this job description resonates with you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of the requirements below. We’re interested in getting to know you and what you bring to the table!

Personalized benefits that support personal well-being and growth:

JLL recognizes the impact that the workplace can have on your wellness, so we offer a supportive culture and comprehensive benefits package that prioritizes mental, physical and emotional health.

About JLL –

We’re JLL—a leading professional services and investment management firm specializing in real estate. We have operations in over 80 countries and a workforce of over 102,000 individuals around the world who help real estate owners, occupiers and investors achieve their business ambitions. As a global Fortune 500 company, we also have an inherent responsibility to drive sustainability and corporate social responsibility. That’s why we’re committed to our purpose to shape the future of real estate for a better world. We’re using the most advanced technology to create rewarding opportunities, amazing spaces and sustainable real estate solutions for our clients, our people, and our communities.

Our core values of teamwork, ethics and excellence are also fundamental to everything we do and we’re honored to be recognized with awards for our success by organizations both globally and locally.

Creating a diverse and inclusive culture where we all feel welcomed, valued and empowered to achieve our full potential is important to who we are today and where we’re headed in the future. And we know that unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives help us think bigger, spark innovation and succeed together.

title: Senior/Executive, Business Development & Partnerships
description:
Senior/Executive, Business Development & Partnerships

Singapore Environment Council (SEC)

Grow Sustainability. Grow Your Career.

The Singapore Environment Council (SEC) is an independent, non-profit organisation dedicated to promoting environmental sustainability and responsible business practices. Through certification programmes, sustainability initiatives and stakeholder engagement, SEC works with organisations across industries to drive positive environmental impact.

We are looking for a driven, results-oriented

Senior/Executive, Business Development & Partnerships

to grow SEC's certification, sustainability and advisory business. If you enjoy opening doors, closing deals and building partnerships that create real environmental impact, we would like to hear from you.

If you have a passion for client engagement, business development and sustainability, we would like to hear from you.

About the Role

As a Senior/Executive, Client Engagement & Business Development, you will play an important role in growing SEC's certification and sustainability services. You will engage clients and partners, develop new business opportunities, support agreement development, and provide administrative support to ensure smooth departmental operations.

This is an individual contributor position with sales targets and opportunities to develop expertise in sustainability certification programmes and environmental standards.

Key Responsibilities

Business Development & Sales

Identify, qualify and pursue new business opportunities across SEC's certification, sustainability and advisory service offerings.

Achieve individual sales targets and maintain a healthy pipeline of prospects.

Generate leads through networking, outreach, industry events and targeted campaigns.

Conduct presentations and pitches to organisations interested in SEC's programmes and services.

Build and maintain relationships with new and existing clients to secure renewals and expand business.

Partnerships & Deal Closing

Develop partnerships with industry associations, corporates, government agencies and other stakeholders.

Draft, format and negotiate business agreements, Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) and partnership proposals.

Work with internal stakeholders and external parties to move agreements through review to finalisation.

Maintain accurate records of agreements, proposals and deal status.

Events & Market Presence

Represent SEC at industry events, exhibitions, networking sessions and stakeholder engagement activities.

Support the planning and execution of major SEC events and programmes to generate leads and partnerships.

Business Operations Support

Prepare sales reports, pipeline updates, presentations and management materials.

Coordinate meetings and follow-up actions with the Deputy Director, Client Engagement.

Support departmental projects and initiatives as required.

What We're Looking For

Qualifications & Experience

Diploma or Degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, or a related discipline.

At least 3 years of experience in business development, sales, partnerships or account management, with a track record of meeting targets.

Experience selling services in sustainability, certification, compliance, environmental services, professional services or consulting will be an advantage.

Candidates with strong business development experience but no sustainability background are encouraged to apply; we will help you build that expertise.

Skills & Competencies

Proactive and target-driven, comfortable with prospecting and outreach.

Confident presenter and persuasive communicator, in writing and in person.

Able to draft and negotiate business documents with attention to detail.

Works independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.

Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Word and Excel.

Manages multiple priorities and deadlines in a dynamic environment.

Professional and ethical in handling confidential information.

Additional Information

Occasional regional travel may be required for business development, stakeholder engagement and certification-related activities.

Why Join SEC?

Grow a business that directly advances Singapore's sustainability goals.

Work with organisations across multiple industries to drive positive environmental impact.

Build expertise in sustainability certifications and environmental standards.

Be part of a purpose-driven organisation committed to a more sustainable future.

Opportunities for professional development and career growth.

Diversity & Inclusion

Singapore Environment Council is committed to providing equal employment opportunities. We welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, religion, marital status, caregiving responsibilities, disability status or background. Selection is based on merit, skills, experience and job-related competencies.

Interested applicants are invited to submit a detailed resume outlining their relevant experience and achievements, including sales or partnership results where possible.

Established in 1995, the

Singapore Environment Council (SEC)

is an independently managed, non-profit, non-governmental organisation (NGO) dedicated to fostering a lasting culture of environmental ownership. As an approved

Institution of a Public Character (IPC)

, we serve as a primary catalyst for environmental advocacy and coordinate efforts across Singapore and the region.

We hold a unique position in the global sustainability landscape:

Global Recognition:

We are the only recognised member of the

Global Ecolabelling Network (GEN)

in Singapore, a non-profit association of leading eco-labelling organisations worldwide.

UN Accreditation:

In 2018, the SEC was granted

United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)

accredited environmental NGO status, further amplifying our influence on sustainability issues.

National Impact:

We work closely with government agencies, statutory boards, and industry partners to translate environmental policy into actionable solutions, such as the

Resource Sustainability Act

and

Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)

frameworks.

At SEC, we don't just influence thinking; we drive systemic change. By joining our team, you will be at the heart of Singapore’s transition toward a circular economy and a more sustainable future

title: Senior Associate/Manager, Private Equity Fund

description:

Strong commercial acumen and strategic thinking skills.

Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

Strong written and spoken English.

title: Business Controller, Asia Pacific (D2C & HUB)
description:
CLARINS
Date: Oct 19, 2026

Singapore, SG, 239519

Ready to bring passion into your career?

A global leading skincare and make-up company, Clarins Group is the embodiment of a committed family history, with a fierce passion for innovation and spirit of independence. Its raison d’être is "making life more beautiful, passing on a more beautiful planet".

Operating in more than 150 countries, we are now the number one skincare company in Europe and are accelerating our development on all other continents, particularly in Asia and the Americas.

Because our 8,000 talents are unique, we are committed to promoting diversity in all its forms.

Do you want to help write the next chapter of our story?

We are looking for a Business Controller, Asia Pacific, based in Singapore.

Mission 1: Finance Business Partner - Direct-to-customer (DTC) Channels

In this capacity, the role supports both Ecommerce and Retail channels across the APAC region and is responsible for the following:

Serve as Finance Business Partner to the Regional Ecommerce and Retail teams, supporting KPI tracking through the preparation, consolidation, and analysis of performance reports.
Maintain and oversee the regional Retail financial database, ensuring data integrity and accuracy. Monitor new boutique openings and renovation projects by reviewing business plans for robustness and conducting ongoing performance follow-up.
Prepare and deliver dedicated quarterly Retail and Ecommerce performance reports for the APAC region, providing clear insights into operational and financial results.
Consolidate monthly APAC Ecommerce and Retail P&L statements, analyzing significant variances against budget and reforecasts, and highlighting key discrepancies and risks.
Act as the primary point of contact for Headquarters Controlling on all Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) financial matters, ensuring alignment and timely communication.
Communicate and implement Group DTC guidelines and requirements across APAC markets, ensuring consistent and rigorous application.

Mission 2: Finance Business Partner – Regional Supply Chain

Within this scope, the Business Controller, APAC is responsible for the following:

Act as Finance Business Partner to the Regional Supply Chain function and serve as the key point of contact for Headquarters Logistics Controlling, in coordination with the RFPAD.
Oversee and review market reporting submissions relating to Inventories and Purchases, ensuring timely, accurate, and complete submissions for both actuals and budget cycles. Serve as the primary contact for APAC markets on related reporting matters.
Prepare consolidated APAC inventory reporting for regional management, covering resale and POP inventories, including provisions and destructions, and provide detailed variance analysis.
Develop and monitor the monthly APAC year-end stock landing forecast, investigating and documenting any deviations versus budget to ensure inventory levels remain aligned with plan.
Analyze stock equations for the Regional Hub and each APAC subsidiary during budget and reforecast cycles, challenging underlying assumptions to ensure completeness and accuracy of purchase projections and cost of goods sold forecasts.
Prepare and review monthly HFM/DMP reporting analyses, identifying significant variances and obtaining appropriate explanations from markets.
Support APAC markets in meeting Supply Chain data and reporting requirements, and deliver training and guidance to markets as required to strengthen reporting accuracy, consistency, and compliance.

Mission 3: Controller of the Intercompany P&L – Singapore Hub

Assume full ownership of the intercompany Profit & Loss related to sales transactions between the Hub and APAC markets, with responsibilities including:

Monitor and oversee intercompany transactions between the France-based factory and APAC markets (Hub activity), in close collaboration with the Regional Supply Chain team.
Lead the preparation of the Hub’s Budget and reforecasts, including related reporting to Group, covering intercompany P&L, inventories, and purchases. Ensure alignment with Regional Supply Chain assumptions and reconciliation with consolidated forecasts submitted by APAC subsidiaries.
Partner with Supply Chain to prepare and monitor inventory provisions for Singapore Hub in accordance with Group policies and accounting standards.
Actively contribute to the monthly closing process by ensuring all required journal entries are properly prepared, documented, and communicated to Accounting, particularly regarding provisions, inventory variances, and destructions.
Perform monthly monitoring of intercompany P&L, purchases, and inventory landing versus budget and reforecasts; investigate and analyze deviations, and report findings to the RFPAD.
Allocate and communicate the APAC markets’ share of IAS 38 allocation related to POP at the Singapore Hub.
Manage Singapore Hub intercompany transfer prices within the Group Supply Chain ERP (M3) for Intercompany Sales, including:
Oversee and maintain the pricing structure within the system, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and alignment with Group policies.
Implement and update price lists and billing prices within the commercial system for annual pricing updates, ensuring correct and timely application.
Act as the primary point of contact for subsidiaries on intercompany pricing matters, including follow-up on missing prices required for forecast valuation.

Mission 4: Drive Process Automation & Continuous Improvement

Within the scope of D2C and Hub topics, the Business Controller, APAC is responsible for:

Identifying and driving opportunities for process improvement to reduce manual work, improve data accuracy, and streamline recurring finance processes.
Partnering with Finance, Data, and Technology teams to design streamlined workflows, and implement automation solutions that strengthen data quality and controls. They will translate business requirements into practical improvements, standardize reporting and planning processes, and promote adoption of modern tools and best practices to enable more timely, insight-driven decision-making.

Other responsibilities may be added to the above, which are consistent with the title Business Controller, Asia Pacific, including involvement in additional projects to lead the change in our Clarins organization.

You Have:

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting or a related discipline, with strong numerical aptitude and business acumen.
Minimum 5 years of FP&A or related experience in a sizeable organisation, preferably within the beauty, retail or FMCG industry and APAC region.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to simplify financial concepts for non-finance stakeholders.
Proactive, adaptable and independent, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate across diverse teams and cultures.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with Workday, HFM, IBM Cognos (BIA), M3 or Power BI is an advantage.

We have:

Over 72 years of expertise in beauty and spa, with the Clarins and myBlend brands
Unique products and innovative services
A commitment to Social & Environmental Responsibility embedded in our raison d’être
A caring and inclusive corporate culture
Development and training opportunities
Attractive compensation and benefits
A flexible work environment, with up to 1 day of remote working per week

If you have a curious mind, a thirst to go further, and the drive to boldly take on new challenges, join us.

title: Business Analyst - Temenos T24 & TAP
description:
Project description

This role will be part of the Platform and Integration Office team, supporting the Group Wealth Platform (GWP) regional rollout programme for Private Banking. GWP is the Group's integrated wealth
management platform built on Temenos Transact (T24) as the core banking and wealth back-office system and Temenos Triple'A Plus (TAP) as the front- and middle-office portfolio management system,
covering client investment account opening, order management and pre-trade checks, wealth product processing, portfolio management, assisted and self-service channels, and downstream data and reporting.
The GWP – Business Analyst, Temenos T24 & TAP Subject Matter Expert (SME) will be the programme's go-to functional expert on the Temenos wealth product suite. The role bridges business requirements
and the Temenos solution, ensuring that business needs are met through standard product capability and model bank configuration wherever possible, and that gaps, customisations and workarounds
are clearly understood, justified and governed.
The ideal candidate will bring deep hands-on knowledge of T24 and TAP, gained through one or more end-to-end Temenos implementations for private banks or wealth managers in the Asia Pacific
(APAC) market. He/she will apply this experience to fit-gap analysis, solution design review, T24–TAP integration, data migration, testing and go-live readiness across markets at different stages of rollout,
while also advising on APAC market practices and local regulatory needs.
The candidate is expected to demonstrate strong discipline in business analysis and documentation, and to be able to work well within a team and yet take initiative and ownership over his/her own area of work assignments or projects.

Responsibilities

Act as the functional SME for Temenos T24 and TAP across the programme, advising business and project teams on standard product capability, model bank configuration and industry best practice for private banking and wealth management.

Lead requirement workshops and fit-gap analysis against T24 and TAP, and translate business needs into Business Requirement Documents (BRD), process flows and business rules that are aligned with Temenos capability; recommend configuration-first solutions and challenge unnecessary customisation.

Review Functional Specification Documents (FSD) and solution designs with IT business analysts, architects, Temenos and implementation partners; independently challenge and validate IT's proposed T24 and TAP solutions, customisations, workarounds and effort estimates to ensure they are fit-for-purpose, aligned to standard product capability and meet business intent, and drive closure of requirement gaps and deviations.

Provide T24 functional expertise across customer and account set-up, securities and portfolio (SC), funds, bonds, FX, money market and deposits, corporate actions, fees and charges, safekeeping, settlement, accounting and wealth financing / lending (e.g. Lombard and overdraft facilities).

Provide TAP functional expertise across portfolio and mandate set-up, advisory and discretionary portfolio management (DPM), model portfolios and rebalancing, order management, pre-trade and investment compliance checks, suitability and risk profiling, performance measurement and client reporting.

Define and validate integration requirements between T24, TAP and surrounding systems such as order management, channels, market data, custodians and brokers, payments, and downstream data, finance and regulatory reporting, including interface timing, data ownership and reconciliation.

Support data migration by defining T24 and TAP data mapping, transformation rules and reconciliation criteria for clients, portfolios, positions, cash balances and static data, and by validating mock and dress rehearsal migration results.

Formulate SIT and UAT scope, end-to-end test scenarios and test cases across the T24 and TAP trade and portfolio lifecycle; support test execution, defect triage and root-cause analysis, and coordinate business sign-off.

Support go-live operational readiness, cutover and hypercare, including SOP updates, user roles and entitlement design, production issue triage, and handover of accepted gaps and enhancements into the BAU platform backlog.

Advise on APAC market localisation for new market rollouts, including local product features, market and settlement practices, tax and regulatory reporting needs, and assess their impact on the regional T24 and TAP baseline.

Prepare training material and user guides on T24 and TAP functions, deliver knowledge transfer to business users, operations and junior business analysts, and build internal Temenos capability within the team.

Build and maintain strong relationships with business units, technology teams, operations, compliance, Temenos and implementation partners; communicate progress, decisions and risks clearly to stakeholders at various levels of the organisation.

Skills

Must have

Bachelor's degree in Banking and Finance, Business Administration, Information Systems, Computer Science or a related field.

Minimum 8 years of experience in banking IT or business analysis, including at least 5 years of hands-on experience with Temenos Transact (T24) and Temenos Triple'A Plus (TAP) in private banking or wealth management.

Proven track record of at least one full-lifecycle T24 and/or TAP implementation in the APAC market (e.g. Singapore, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia or other Asian markets), from requirements and fit-gap through to go-live and post-implementation support.

In-depth functional knowledge of T24 wealth-related modules (e.g. Securities (SC), Arrangement Architecture (AA), FX, Money Market, Derivatives (DX), Corporate Actions, Lending) and of TAP portfolio management, order management, investment compliance and reporting capabilities.

Proven ability to challenge and validate IT T24 solution designs, including functional specifications, parameter and configuration set-up, local developments and interface designs, and to assess whether proposed solutions are fit-for-purpose, efficient and aligned with Temenos standard capability. Prior experience as an IT Business Analyst on T24 implementations will be a strong plus.

Solid wealth management product knowledge across bonds, equities, mutual funds, FX, structured products, deposits and wealth financing, including the trade lifecycle, booking, settlement, valuation and accounting flows.

Hands-on experience in data migration, SIT/UAT and cutover for core banking or wealth platform implementations.

Familiarity with APAC private banking market practices and regulatory requirements (e.g. MAS, HKMA, OJK) relevant to wealth products and client suitability.

Strong knowledge of delivery methodologies (e.g. Agile, Waterfall) and tools (e.g. JIRA, Confluence, MS Project).

Excellent analytical, problem-solving and documentation skills, with the ability to explain complex Temenos functions in clear business terms.

Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills; able to work independently across multiple markets and locations, and willing to travel within the region as required.

Nice to have

Temenos product certification (T24 / Transact or Triple'A Plus / Wealth) is highly desirable

Bbusiness analysis or project management certification (e.g. CBAP, PMP, Agile/Scrum) is an advantage.

Good understanding of T24–TAP integration and data flows, and familiarity with Temenos integration tools (e.g. Temenos Integration Framework, OFS, APIs) is an advantage.

Experience with T24 upgrades or Temenos Wealth / WealthSuite is a plus.

title: Senior Marketing & Communications Specialist
description:
Overview

ENGIE is a global energy company, a leading provider of electricity, natural gas, and energy services. With 100 000 employees in more than 70 countries worldwide, ENGIE achieved revenue of €95 billion in 2023. ENGIE is committed to being a leader in the energy transition. We are looking for talented and motivated people to create the future of energy. Join a rewarding and flexible work environment that encourages innovation and creativity, and help us meet the energy challenges of today and tomorrow.

The Supply & Energy Management (S&EM) Global Business Unit covers trading and risk management activities as well as B2B and B2C supply activities across a large and highly diversified energy portfolio, including electricity, natural gas, biomass, LNG and other fuels, CO2 and environmental products

Within the S&EM Business Unit, Business Platform APAC is developing ENGIE’s trading and risk management activities across the APAC region, Middle East and India, around 4 main pillars: risk management and market access, asset management, green solutions and energy supply businesses.

Purpose

The Senior Marketing & Communications Specialist supports the development and delivery of integrated marketing and communications activities that strengthen ENGIE’s Supply & Energy Management positioning and business growth across Asia.The role serves as a regional principal Marketing and Communications focal point of contact for S&EM activities across markets in the region, including Singapore and Japan, working closely ensuring consistency of S&EM’s positioning and coordinating with the relevant Country, GBU and Group Communications teams to ensure consistent messaging, brand alignment and effective execution in accordance with the ENGIE Communications operating model. Communications accountability in individual markets remains with the respective Country Communications teams.

The role contributes to positioning ENGIE as a credible partner in energy supply, renewable energy solutions, corporate PPAs, environmental products, energy management and decarbonisation. Working with commercial, trading and business development teams, the role supports market-facing campaigns, thought leadership, customer engagement initiatives and communications materials that build visibility and enable business development.

Key Responsibilities

Business marketing and commercial support: Support the planning and execution of marketing and communications activities aligned with S&EM growth objectives; work with commercial and business development teams to develop customer-facing materials; and prepare sales-enablement content, presentations, business profiles and solution collateral.

Thought leadership and market positioning: Support and in the development of markets relevant to S&EM’s regional activities and client coverage market insights, executive viewpoints, case studies, industry articles and customer success stories; work with subject matter experts to translate complex market and trading topics into clear, engaging content for customers and internal stakeholders.

External communications and reputation: Support proactive communications activities linked to S&EM business priorities; draft and coordinate media materials, press releases, industry submissions and external messaging; monitor relevant industry developments and support issues management preparation when required.

Digital marketing and content: Manage and produce content for websites, LinkedIn and other relevant channels; maintain an S&EM editorial calendar aligned to commercial priorities; develop campaign assets, newsletters, infographics, videos and presentations; and track engagement and campaign performance indicators.

Events and customer engagement: Coordinate communications and marketing support for industry conferences, customer forums, webinars, roundtables and trade exhibitions; prepare event content, key messages and engagement materials; and support regional customer engagement initiatives.

Internal communications: Prepare internal communications materials that build awareness of S&EM’s activities, products and capabilities across ENGIE; support leadership communications, employee engagement content and regional announcements.

Brand and governance: Ensure communications and marketing materials follow ENGIE brand standards; coordinate with ENGIE Group and regional communications teams; and apply established communications review and approval processes.

Qualifications, skills and experience

Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Public Relations, Journalism or a related discipline.

Professional communications, digital marketing or brand-related certification would be advantageous.

Technical Skills & Experience

4 years’ experience in B2B marketing, communications, corporate affairs, digital marketing or a related field.

Exposure to power, utilities, energy trading, renewable energy, sustainability, infrastructure or related sectors would be advantageous.

Good understanding of commercial marketing, customer engagement and business development support.

Experience assisting with thought leadership content, digital campaigns, customer-facing communications materials and executive presentations.

Strong writing, editing, messaging and storytelling capability, with the ability to simplify technical energy and market topics for different audiences.

Ability to coordinate with stakeholders across commercial, trading, leadership, communications and regional teams.

Competencies

Clear communication and business partnering mindset.

Commercial awareness and ability to connect marketing activities to business priorities.

Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills.

Creativity, curiosity and ability to develop compelling market-facing narratives.

High attention to detail, brand discipline and governance mindset.

Ability to work independently while seeking alignment in a regional, matrixed environment.

ENGIE Energy Marketing Singapore Pte Ltd

ENGIE Energy Marketing Singapore Pte Ltd is the LNG trading platform at the heart of ENGIE, a global energy player in the three businesses of gas, power and energy services, and a comprehensive presence throughout the energy value chain.

Combining in-depth industry experience and financial-market know-how, we serve with LNG solutions all ENGIE business activities worldwide and trade LNG with third parties, from upstream producers to downstream utilities.

ENGIE Energy Marketing Singapore Pte Ltd also has a local presence in Europe (Paris, London, and Madrid).

Unequivocally client-focused, we bring the best of both worlds – energy and trading – to our business partners, be they within the Group or external customers.

title: Chief Executive Officer
description:
Job Summary

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will be responsible for the overall strategic direction, business performance and management of the company. The role involves driving sustainable business growth, improving profitability, overseeing F&B operations, developing new business opportunities and ensuring operational excellence across the organisation.

The successful candidate will provide strategic leadership, strengthen the company's market position, build a high-performing management team and ensure that business objectives are achieved in line with the company's vision and long-term goals.

Key Responsibilities

1. Business Strategy and Development

Develop and implement short-term and long-term business strategies to achieve the company's growth, revenue and profitability objectives.

Identify new business opportunities, market trends and expansion strategies, including new outlets, brands, franchising and strategic partnerships where applicable.

Evaluate business performance and implement initiatives to strengthen market competitiveness and business sustainability.

Establish corporate objectives, performance targets and key performance indicators (KPIs) for the organisation.

2. F&B Operations Management

Oversee the overall operations of the company's restaurants, central kitchens and other F&B business units, where applicable.

Establish and implement standard operating procedures (SOPs) to improve productivity, operational consistency and service delivery.

Monitor outlet performance and implement improvements to optimise manpower utilisation, inventory management and operating costs.

Oversee menu development, product innovation, pricing strategies and quality control in collaboration with relevant teams.

3. Financial Management and Profitability

Take overall responsibility for the company's financial performance, including revenue growth, profit and loss (P&L), budgeting and cash flow management.

Develop annual budgets, financial forecasts and business plans.

Monitor food costs, labour costs, rental expenses, procurement costs and other operating expenses to improve profitability.

Review financial reports and operational results, identify areas for improvement and implement cost-control measures.

Evaluate capital expenditure, investments and new business proposals to ensure sound financial returns.

4. Leadership and Human Resource Management

Provide leadership and strategic direction to senior management, department heads and outlet operations teams.

Oversee manpower planning, recruitment, succession planning, staff development and performance management.

Build a strong organisational culture that promotes accountability, teamwork, productivity and service excellence.

Establish clear performance expectations and develop management capabilities to support business growth.

Ensure effective communication and coordination across departments.

5. Sales, Marketing and Brand Management

Develop and oversee sales, marketing and promotional strategies to increase revenue, customer acquisition and brand awareness.

Strengthen the company's brand positioning and market presence through effective marketing initiatives and customer engagement.

Monitor customer feedback, market developments and competitor activities to identify opportunities for improvement.

Explore new sales channels, strategic collaborations and digital platforms to expand the customer base.

6. Supply Chain and Procurement

Oversee procurement strategies, supplier relationships and supply chain management to ensure reliable sourcing and competitive pricing.

Negotiate with suppliers and business partners to optimise purchasing costs and maintain product quality.

Ensure effective inventory management and minimise food wastage, stock losses and supply disruptions.

Maintain appropriate supplier performance standards and implement cost-efficient procurement practices.

7. Regulatory Compliance and Risk Management

Ensure the company's operations comply with applicable Singapore laws, regulations, licensing requirements and industry standards.

Oversee compliance with relevant Singapore Food Agency (SFA) food safety and hygiene requirements, Ministry of Manpower (MOM) employment regulations and workplace safety requirements.

Ensure appropriate risk management, internal controls and business continuity measures are in place.

Monitor regulatory changes and implement the necessary policies, procedures and corrective actions.

Safeguard the company's reputation, assets and business interests.

8. Corporate Governance and Stakeholder Management

Report business performance, strategic developments and key risks to the Board of Directors or shareholders, where applicable.

Build and maintain strong relationships with investors, business partners, landlords, suppliers, customers and relevant authorities.

Represent the company in negotiations, strategic partnerships and key business engagements.

Ensure responsible decision-making and effective governance in accordance with the company's objectives and policies.

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Management, Hospitality, Food & Beverage or related field.

Minimum 5 years of relevant management experience, preferably in catering, food distribution or F&B.

Extensive senior management experience in the food and beverage, hospitality or related industry.

Proven track record in business leadership, strategic planning, revenue growth and profitability management.

Strong experience in financial management, budgeting, P&L analysis and cost optimisation.

Experience overseeing multi-outlet operations, business expansion or new business development is an advantage.

Good knowledge of F&B operations, food safety standards and the Singapore regulatory environment.

Strong leadership, strategic thinking, negotiation and decision-making skills.

Excellent communication, interpersonal and stakeholder management abilities.

Results-oriented, commercially driven and capable of leading teams in a fast-paced business environment.

Good command of English

title: Flint Asia-Pacific Data Centres Manager / Associate Director
description:
We are looking for a 

Manager

or

Associate Director

with experience related to

data centres

to support the delivery of client work and business development work across our fast-growing

Asia-Pacific

team based in

Singapore

.

You will work closely with team members to support our data centre clients on public policy, regulation, politics, and commercial strategy. There may also be opportunities to work with Flint’s other tech sector clients.

Data centre operators face a challenging policy and regulatory environment across Asia-Pacific. AI and cloud-based demand is driving rapid growth and investment, but delivering a return on this capital is becoming more complicated. In parts of the region, concerns over data centres’ impact on communities, on infrastructure, and on the environment are leading to policy change that impacts on how operators build and operate data centres. We are helping investors and operators of data centres to build understanding of the benefits they bring and to make the case to governments for policy frameworks that enable the growth of the sector.

You will have scope to engage with clients at the most senior levels. The role will provide an unparalleled opportunity to research and analyse the complex policy and political challenges our clients face and develop options and approaches to address those challenges, backing up recommendations with wider strategic and political analysis.

Flint provides an excellent professional and educational environment for people to accelerate their personal and career development. There will be space to engage in discussion and debates on substantive policy and political challenges, as well as significant scope for progression through the company.

You will join a rapidly growing team, with the opportunity to take ownership of tasks and contribute to the company’s growth in the region.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for candidates who have

experience

relevant to

data centre policy

. Relevant issues include power availability and grid connection, permitting and licensing, water, sustainability, cybersecurity and resilience, and community sentiment and social licence to operate.

We are not expecting candidates to have expertise in all of the above

.

We welcome any candidates with experience working in relevant roles in the data centre sector, government departments, regulators, research firms, or other advisory roles. We will consider candidates from a range of functional backgrounds, including those with more technical industry backgrounds. For

Manager / Associate Director level

roles, we will consider candidates with a range of experience - from

4 - 9 years’ work experience –

though this is a

guide

only and we will consider applications on a case-by-case basis.

Our ideal candidate will have:

Strong experience relevant to data centre policy.

The skills required to work on policy and regulation – the ability to research and analyse complex policy issues and to draft policy positions in a clear and structured way.

A professional background in the data centre sector, government, a regulator, consultancy, think tank, or industry body in managerial positions.

A proven track record of managing projects and teams in fast-paced, delivery-focused environments.

Strong interpersonal skills – a flexible approach and the ability to work well across teams, both with colleagues and clients.

Commercial acumen, with the ability to identify new business opportunities and deliver commercially viable solutions to clients.

Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the ability to provide clear, concise advice to stakeholders, both in written and verbal form.

(desirable but not required) Connections to government officials and / or regulators working on data centre-related policy in at least one Asia-Pacific country or multilateral grouping.

TO APPLY

To be successful, please submit your

CV

with a short

cover letter

(max 600 words) by

Friday 30 October

. Use your cover letter to explain how your background is relevant to the role and

include at least one paragraph on the policy and regulatory challenges facing the data centre sector in the Asia-Pacific region.

STANDINGOUT

To be successful, please submit your CV and cover letter setting out:

Why you would like to join Flint.

How your experience and skills qualify you for this specific role and its requirements.

The policy and regulatory challenges facing the data centre sector in the Asia-Pacific region.

Whether you have the right to work in Singapore.

Your possible start date and salary expectation.

We will

review applications as they arrive

and may invite candidates to interview before the closing date.

ABOUT FLINT

Flint is a leading global strategy consultancy with a focus on policy, politics, regulation, and economics. We are advisers to some of the largest corporates, financial institutions, and investors in Europe and the Asia-Pacific. We work at the point where government and business meet, drawing on our blend of international expertise and experience to offer an authoritative perspective on both.

We have offices in London, Brussels, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Melbourne, as well as in a number of European capitals. We have also established a network of senior advisers across key Asia-Pacific markets. We offer successful candidates the opportunity to advance within the company.

Flint takes care of its people. We enjoy challenging each other’s thinking and working hard on a wide variety of interesting and stimulating projects, while simultaneously respecting life outside Flint. We offer a flexible working environment with global health insurance coverage and 25 days of holiday accrued from your start date.

We are committed to equality of opportunity for all staff and applications from individuals are encouraged regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships.

P.T. Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, is a leading Indonesian bank providing comprehensive corporate banking solutions to support business growth and financial needs. The role supports business growth by enhancing client relationships, optimizing loan portfolio distribution, improving balance sheet management, and providing market intelligence and advisory services to Management and Credit Committees.

The position works closely with Overseas Branches (KLN), Head Office, borrowers, investors, and financial institutions to execute syndicated loan transactions and support strategic business initiatives.

1. Loan Origination & Lead Arranger Activities

Support Overseas Branches (KLN) in identifying and originating syndicated loan opportunities.

Develop target client lists aligned with the Bank’s risk appetite and business strategy.

Support internal credit approval processes through preparation of credit papers and presentations.

Build and maintain relationships with corporate clients, financial institutions, and key market participants.

Provide independent market views regarding deal structure, pricing, syndication progress, and risk considerations.

Support bookrunning and syndication efforts across Corporate Banking, Financial Institutions, Non-Bank Financial Institutions, and Overseas Branch portfolios.

Develop and maintain relationships with regional and international investor banks.

Identify distribution opportunities to optimize portfolio management and balance sheet utilization.

Facilitate loan sell-down activities to improve capital efficiency and enhance return on equity (ROE).

Provide origination ideas that align with market demand and investor appetite.

Monitor developments in the syndicated loan market and provide regular market updates.

Analyze sector trends, banking liquidity, investor appetite, pricing benchmarks, and comparable transactions.

Prepare investor call reports and market intelligence updates for senior management.

Advise business units, management, and Credit Committees on market conditions, transaction structures, pricing strategy, and syndication feasibility.

Contribute to strategic decision-making by providing insights into market trends and transaction opportunities.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Banking, Economics, Business Administration, Accounting, or a related discipline.

Strong knowledge of syndicated lending, corporate banking, structured finance, credit analysis, and loan documentation.

Good understanding of financial markets, credit risk assessment, and portfolio management.

Strong financial modeling and financial statement analysis skills.

Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

Experience

5-10 years of relevant experience

in syndicated loans, corporate banking, investment banking, structured finance, credit analysis, debt capital markets, or loan distribution.

Proven track record in originating, structuring, executing, or distributing syndicated loan transactions.

Experience in managing complex financing transactions involving multiple stakeholders.

Familiarity with internal credit approval processes and presentations to senior management and credit committees.

Experience working with borrowers, financial institutions, investors, legal counsel, and external arrangers.

Regional or international banking experience, particularly in cross-border transactions, is highly desirable.

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple transactions simultaneously under tight deadlines.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Excellent negotiation and stakeholder management capabilities.

Strong commercial acumen and business development mindset.

Ability to build and maintain relationships with clients and market participants.

Effective presentation and communication skills.

High attention to detail and strong project management capabilities.

Sound judgment, integrity, and commitment to regulatory and compliance standards.

description:

Embracing a strong ecosystem of global partners, NCS transforms technology services delivery combining AI with digital resilience to drive real business impact. Job Description

The ideal candidate is a senior product leader who can operate confidently at both strategic and execution levels. They are comfortable influencing senior stakeholders, making prioritisation decisions across competing demands, and creating structure without slowing delivery. They bring credibility through deep product management experience, consulting discipline, and strong pre-sales and solutioning expertise, with the ability to shape client problem statements, develop compelling solution approaches, and connect business goals with practical delivery outcomes. They also have the maturity to work across public and private sector contexts, where governance, risk, value, and stakeholder complexity may differ.

The role holder is responsible for leading a portfolio of products or strategic product initiatives to deliver measurable business value, strong client outcomes, and scalable product practices across teams. This role combines product leadership, portfolio prioritisation, operating model design, governance, analytics, and executive engagement. They are also expected to bring thought leadership, mentor teams, and contribute to organisation-wide product management best practices.

What will you do:

1. Lead portfolio delivery and maximise impact

Lead a portfolio of products, product streams, or strategic initiatives from planning through delivery and value realisation.
Ensure product teams are focused on solving the highest-value problems for users, clients, and the business.
Translate strategic priorities into clear product outcomes, roadmaps, and delivery plans across multiple squads.
Drive alignment between business objectives, user needs, delivery capacity, and technical feasibility.
Monitor whether delivered initiatives achieve intended outcomes, and intervene when priorities, scope, or execution need adjustment.
Balance short-term delivery commitments with long-term product sustainability, platform health, and strategic growth.
Guide teams to move beyond feature delivery and maintain focus on measurable impact, adoption, and product performance.

2. Establish product operating model and governance across squads; scale product discovery and measurement

Define, implement, and continuously improve the product operating model across squads to ensure consistency, clarity, and accountability.
Establish clear governance mechanisms for product planning, decision-making, prioritisation, dependency management, and escalation.
Clarify roles, responsibilities, and decision rights across product, engineering, design, delivery, architecture, and business stakeholders.
Standardise core product management practices such as discovery, roadmap planning, backlog management, experimentation, and outcome tracking.
Scale effective product discovery practices so squads consistently validate user needs, business value, and solution assumptions before delivery.
Ensure squads use suitable measures of success, including discovery metrics, delivery indicators, adoption measures, and value outcomes.
Promote disciplined yet practical governance that enables speed, transparency, and quality decision-making rather than unnecessary process.

3. Shape investment and prioritisation across a portfolio; influence executive stakeholders

Lead portfolio-level prioritisation by assessing strategic fit, value potential, cost, risk, dependency, and execution readiness.
Develop structured business cases, investment proposals, and prioritisation recommendations for senior leadership review.
Work with executives and cross-functional leaders to align investment decisions with enterprise goals, client priorities, regulatory considerations, and delivery realities.
Support trade-off discussions where funding, resources, timelines, or business priorities are constrained.
Communicate portfolio choices, sequencing logic, and expected outcomes in a clear and credible manner to senior stakeholders.
Influence decision-making through evidence, market insight, user understanding, and commercial judgement.

4. Define product analytics strategy and value realisation system

Establish a product analytics approach that supports decision-making at squad, product, and portfolio levels.
Define and implement value realisation frameworks using OKRs, product health metrics, adoption measures, customer outcomes, operational indicators, and commercial impact metrics where relevant.
Ensure product teams have clear baselines, targets, and review cadences to track whether products are delivering intended value.
Partner with data, engineering, and business teams to improve access to quality data and strengthen product insight capability.
Use analytics to identify opportunities, underperformance, risks, and improvement actions across the portfolio.
Create regular reporting and review mechanisms for leadership to assess progress, product health, and return on investment.
Promote a culture of evidence-based decision-making and continuous learning.

5. Provide thought leadership and shape organisational best practice

Act as a senior product leader who brings strong point of view, practical experience, and market-informed thinking to improve product management maturity across the organisation.
Contribute to development of product frameworks, standards, governance models, and playbooks.
Coach and mentor product managers and cross-functional teams to strengthen product capability and consistency of practice.
Share lessons learned, emerging trends, and proven approaches to improve how teams deliver product outcomes.
Support leadership in building a stronger product culture and embedding best practice across business and delivery teams.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate should possess:

More than 15 years of experience across product management and consulting, including leadership responsibility for complex products, portfolios, or transformation initiatives.
Demonstrated experience leading product strategy, delivery, and value realisation across multiple squads or business domains.
Proven experience in project and product delivery in both government and commercial environments.
Strong experience in portfolio prioritisation, business case development, investment shaping, and executive stakeholder management.
Experience designing or improving product operating models, governance structures, and scalable product practices.
Hands-on experience in product discovery, roadmap management, experimentation, and outcome measurement.
Strong track record in defining and using OKRs, product health metrics, and analytics to drive product decisions and business outcomes.
Experience working with cross-functional teams including engineering, design, architecture, data, operations, and senior business stakeholders.
Proven experience in pre-sales and solutioning, including shaping client problem statements, developing product and delivery approaches, contributing to proposals and business cases, and presenting solution recommendations to senior stakeholders

Relevant Certifications:

Product management certification is required. Examples may include recognised certifications in product management, product ownership, or digital product leadership.
Agile, Scrum, Lean, or related delivery certifications are advantageous.

title: Program Origination & Marketing Manager
description:
Company Overview

The Singapore Mint, established in 1968, has evolved into a leading innovative mint producing high-quality coins, medallions, and collectibles. It combines advanced technology with skilled craftsmanship and serves both local and international markets.

Job Summary

The Manager, Programme Origination leads the team to develop and execute commemorative coin and collectible product programmes, owning strategy, marketing, delivery, and P&L to achieve commercial and performance targets.

Responsibilities

Lead and manage the Programme Origination team to deliver product programmes that meet yearly margin targets and enhance team capabilities in a dynamic environment

Plan, execute, and review programmes managing scope, schedule, budget, quality, launch readiness, risks, and post-launch performance

Conduct market research to identify trends and originate differentiated product concepts that enhance brand equity

Oversee marketing and communications plans, including product storytelling, campaign briefs, sales enablement materials, and channel support across retail, e-commerce, corporate sales, and digital platforms

Coordinate internal teams across programme origination, marketing, sales, design, production, and operations to ensure aligned delivery and accountability

Manage external contractors, agencies, vendors, and partners to deliver quality, cost, timelines, messaging, and brand standards

Monitor programme KPIs and P&L, track sales, margin, and engagement targets, and implement timely corrective actions

Provide accurate programme reporting, documentation, and management updates

Recommend programme concepts, timelines, budget allocations, go-to-market requirements, and risk mitigation or performance improvement actions

Influence cross-functional delivery across marketing, production, operations, sales, and external partners to ensure cohesive execution

The Singapore Mint was established in 1968 to mint circulation coins for the newly-independent nation. Over the years, The Singapore Mint has evolved from a basic minting facility to a fully integrated business operation, comprising programme concept, product design, marketing, sales and distribution with after sales service. Focusing on quality system and standards, The Singapore Mint is a certified ISO 9001 and 14001 organisation. Today, it has grown to become one of the leading innovative mints in the industry, capable of producing coins and medallions of the highest quality.

Leveraging on technology, The Singapore Mint has developed hybrid techniques to create high security and innovative features on circulation and commemorative coins and collectables. Fusing advanced minting technologies with authentic crafting methods, The Singapore Mint is one of the few mints in the world that still maintains a team of highly skilled craftsmen, adding intricate elements that can only be meticulously achieved by the human touch.

As a testament of its high quality crafting techniques, The Singapore Mint has won multiple international awards and its rising stature has garnered much interest internationally. The mint has been appointed by issuing authorities around the world for the production of their coins.

Other than producing coins and medallions, The Singapore Mint has also expanded to provide quality currency-related gifts and collectibles, lifestyle products and services to both local and international markets. We continue to pledge our unwavering commitment to our customers, business associates and partners to offer the best in quality, value and service.

The Singapore Mint (Singapore Precision Industries Pte Ltd) is a fully owned subsidiary of Sembcorp Industries.
