title: Partnerships Director, Visa Government Solutions, Asia Pacific
description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Team Summary

Visa Government Solutions (VGS) leads the company efforts to build a business for public sector sales by working with issuer and acquiring banks and other ecosystem partners to solve complex public sector payments challenges that deliver economic, social, and efficiency benefits to individuals and businesses. You will be an integral part of the global VGS team. The role will be based in our Asia Pacific Market Support Centre in Singapore and report directly into the Go-to-Market and Commercialisation lead for VGS Asia Pacific.

What's exciting about joining the Visa Government Solutions team?



- You will partner with government technology providers, system integrators, fintechs, and development organisations to develop and deliver innovative and high impact payments solutions for the public sector. 
- We’re a key part of Visa’s focus on new payment flows as a growth driver for our business. 
- The nature of this sector reinforces Visa’s purpose-led brand values with social and economic impact. 

What a Director of Partnerships for Government Solutions does at Visa:

Visa is seeking an experienced professional to develop and scale strategic commercial relationships for Visa Government Solutions with ecosystem enabler partners, including government technology providers (digital government platforms, system integrators, software solutions, fintechs), providers of specialist capabilities in sector / industry verticals, and humanitarian and development organisations.

Working closely with Visa’s various products and solutions teams, this role will scale enabler partnerships as a key route to market by combining Visa and partner capabilities to deliver innovative public sector solutions and accelerate commercial growth across Asia Pacific.

The Role Encompasses The Following Responsibilities



- Expand and execute our ecosystem partnership sales strategy in collaboration with in-market VGS Sales teams across the region and global VGS colleagues, creating a prioritized pipeline of partners, solutions and commercial opportunities. 
- Identify public sector use cases and complementary joint solutions that can be built or scaled to unlock incremental revenue for Visa and ecosystem partners. This may include requirements for Visa solutions teams to incorporate into product and solutions roadmaps. 
- Support VGS in-market sales leads to identify, structure and execute mutually beneficial local partnerships with commercial or strategic agreements that can lead to the growth of VGS business, and onboard suppliers accordingly. 
- Own and manage partnerships with organisations that are either ready to scale or already operating across multiple Asia Pacific markets. Develop and execute sales strategies / account plans, contracting and onboarding as required with these strategic multi-market ecosystem partners to increase sales volume and market share. 
- Support the development of RFP strategies and responses with strategic partners. 
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders on partner outreach strategy, targets, and approach to educating influencers on how VGS can support the public sector. 
- Develop and articulate compelling value propositions for internal and external audiences, positioning VGS as a leader in the payments industry for Governments and a resource for ecosystem partners. 
- Proactively identify and resolve issues affecting partnership sales execution, while monitoring market developments and recommending new approaches to grow the VGS business. 
- Stay updated on latest developments in the Govtech space, with a strategic focus on identifying new growth verticals. 

Why This Is Important To Visa

This role is critical to building enabler partnerships that scale Visa Government Solutions across Asia Pacific markets. Governments play an important and increasing role in the lives of citizens and businesses. Government payments are a significant part of this, be it government making payments to suppliers or social payments in form of disbursements or accepting tax payments from citizens. In some instances, Governments are also leading the way in payments innovation, such as Government digital transformation, Central Bank Digital Currencies, stablecoins, AI, open data, and in dealing with the big challenges of our times (climate, sustainability). We are looking to partner with Governments around the world as they drive ambitious plans for economic growth, social impact and digitalization, and our ecosystem partners are an important part of how we can elevate payments innovation.

This is a hybrid position. Expectation of days in office will be confirmed by your hiring manager.

Qualifications

What you will need:



- 12+ years’ experience working in, or with, organisations that provide technology, infrastructure or other specialist capabilities to governments, ideally with additional payments expertise. 
- Track record and proven ability to drive commercial outcomes and grow a business through strategic partnerships. 
- Robust understanding of how public sector sales and public agencies operate with expertise in navigating government agencies and procedures, including government procurement. 
- Experience structuring partnership deals, with the technical fluency to lead discussions with ecosystem partners and to articulate value propositions across a broad portfolio of solutions. 
- Proficiency in onboarding and managing partner relationships, with strong troubleshooting, problem-solving skills, and a bias for action and execution. 
- Consultative sales experience and skillful in developing, negotiating, influencing and selling new partnership synergies to ecosystem partners. 
- Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills required to influence cross-functional teams in internal solution development and go-to-market strategy. 
- Strategic and analytical thinker who is hands-on, and with an entrepreneurial ability that includes comfort with ambiguity and challenges the status quo. 
- Experience working in cross-functional and cross-cultural teams in a matrixed environment. 
- Comfortable speaking at external events to help build Visa’s presence and reputation through thought leadership. 
- Executive communication skills (written, oral & presentation) with an ability to explain complex business and technical concepts to broad audiences in an approachable way 
- Fluent in English. Any additional Asian language a plus. 

What Will Also Help



- Active network of ecosystem partners and public sector stakeholders across Asia. 
- Prior sales and consulting experience servicing government clients and projects. 
- Knowledge of payment solutions relevant to the ecosystem mentioned. 

Visa is an EEO Employer

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

The fintech partnerships team works closely with Visa’s Product and Solutions teams (functions and services) to identify and pursue a new client base of Issuing & Acquiring platforms and various service providers and ecosystem participants in the payments industry across Asia Pacific.

What a Director, Fintech Partnerships Does At Visa

The Director, Fintech Partnerships is responsible for driving end-to-end partnership growth across the Singapore fintech ecosystem, from opportunity identification and business development through solution design, commercial structuring and commercialization.

This role requires a recognized fintech and payments specialist with deep market knowledge, strong industry connections and a proven ability to create new business opportunities. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing strategic partnerships that accelerate adoption of Visa's capabilities while delivering mutual growth for Visa and its partners.

Given the rapid evolution of digital money movement, the candidate should be well versed in stablecoins, tokenized payments, and the broader digital asset ecosystem. They should possess a strong understanding of the regulatory landscape, emerging business models, and the role stablecoins can play in cross-border payments, treasury, settlement, and programmable commerce. The individual will be expected to identify, develop and commercialize partnerships with stablecoin issuers, digital asset platforms, wallets, infrastructure providers and other ecosystem participants that align with Visa's strategic priorities.

While the primary market focus is Singapore, the role may support selected opportunities across Asia Pacific where ecosystem relationships, partnerships or growth opportunities align with Visa's strategic priorities.

Key Responsibilities Will Include

Strategic Account Management and Business Development Ecosystem Growth:



- Own and manage key fintech and digital asset client relationships, ensuring strategic alignment with regional and global priorities while identifying opportunities to deepen partnerships and accelerate business growth
- Identify, develop and execute high-impact partnerships across fintechs, digital banks, payment service providers, embedded finance platforms and emerging ecosystem participants.
- Build strong business development and hunting capabilities to identify new opportunities and emerging business models.
- Leverage industry relationships and ecosystem intelligence to identify opportunities before they become mainstream market initiatives.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with founders, investors, accelerators and ecosystem influencers

Solutioning & Partnership Development



- Work closely with partners to understand customer needs, business models, customer journeys and growth objectives.
- Translate strategic opportunities into scalable payment and commerce solutions leveraging Visa's capabilities.
- Act as a solution integrator by bringing together internal products, services and partners to address client needs.
- Advise internal stakeholders on emerging fintech trends, technologies and ecosystem developments.

Commercialization & Deal Execution



- Lead complex partnership opportunities from origination through negotiation, contracting, launch and revenue realization.
- Build business cases, commercial models and partnership strategies that drive measurable business outcomes.
- Manage a portfolio of fintech relationships to deliver commercial growth and revenue objectives.
- Drive adoption of Visa products and services through partner channels and ecosystem distribution models.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications



- 10+ years of experience in fintech, payments, partnerships, business development, product commercialization or related commercial roles.
- Deep knowledge of the Singapore fintech ecosystem and strong understanding of broader Asia Pacific market developments.
- Proficient in commercial deal modelling, deal negotiation and a proven track record of planning, managing and closing complex deals, with a focus on results driven execution
- Strong understanding of payments, issuing, acquiring, digital wallets, embedded finance, Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS), account-to-account payments and money movement solutions.
- Preference for candidates with prior experience in a global payments organization, scheme network , fintech or related financial institution
- Working knowledge of emerging technologies and payment trends including stablecoins, tokenization, CBDCs, digital assets and programmable payments..
- Ability to assess customer journeys, identify commercial opportunities and translate client needs into scalable payment solutions.
- Proven ability to influence stakeholders and drive outcomes across a matrixed organization.
- Strong executive presence with experience engaging founders, C-suite executives and senior decision makers.
- Entrepreneurial, hands-on and execution-oriented approach with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-changing market.

Visa is an EEO Employer

Working at Abbott

title: Senior Market Strategy and Partnerships Manager
description:
Hey there!

We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

Our team builds trusted, long-term partnerships with leading brands across the ecosystem. We work closely with creators, producers, agencies, and cultural leaders to help them make data-driven decisions, expand their portfolios, and scale internationally. In doing so, we play a key role in shaping the future of the entertainment landscape.

This role goes far beyond relationship management. It requires strong strategic thinking and problem-solving across a wide range of topics, from marketing and pricing to operations and financing. The most successful team members take full ownership of their partners’ success, acting as true partners and advisors at every stage of growth.

Collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. Business Development works hand-in-hand with Marketing, Category Management, Partner Support, Operations, Tech, Product, and Finance to ensure every experience on our platform reaches its full potential.

Our team is diverse, entrepreneurial, and dynamic, bringing together talent from consulting, banking, big tech, and startups. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where creativity meets data, and ambition meets execution.

Join us if you’re passionate about discovering world-class experiences, building meaningful partnerships, and scaling some of the most exciting concepts across the globe.

The Role

In this role, you will drive Fever’s expansion across Singapore's entertainment industry by building and nurturing deep commercial relationships with top producers, creators, venues, and key stakeholders. You will develop and execute an innovative growth strategy to scale our market presence, expertly managing commercial strategies to ensure mutual value creation and build sustainable, long-term partnerships with event organizers. By collaborating closely with cross-functional teams both in Singapore and internationally, you will successfully balance a growing client base while serving as our in-house expert on the coolest trends and newest experiences in the entertainment landscape.

What You'll Do



- Create and cultivate deep business relationships with the biggest producers, creators, venues and key stakeholders in the entertainment industry.
- Develop and deliver a growth strategy for the market, with an innovative and effective approach to scaling Fever's presence in the region
- Expertly manage commercial strategy with large partners ensuring value creation for both parties, and a sustainable strategic partnership between Fever and event organisers
- Evidence strong organizational skills to effectively balance and grow a large base of clients

- Keep up to date with everything cool that’s happening in the entertainment; think of yourself as the expert for new and trending experiences

Who You Are

Here’s what you should bring to the table:



- At least 4+ years of top tier consulting or equivalent experience, with ideally an additional 4+ years of experience in relevant sectors (e.g. corporate management, tech companies, sport / music / arts)
- Strong business development and partnership management skills
- Self-starter mentality with an ability to work in a demanding, dynamic start-up environment
- Demonstrated data-driven approach to business and task prioritization
- Excellent communication skills both written and verbal along with strong attention to detail
- Comfort in working with Microsoft Office, Google docs, and a Sales CRM (Sugar CRM is preferred)

Why You'll Love It Here



- Attractive compensation package consisting of base salary and the potential to earn a significant bonus for top performance.

- Work in WeWork in Singapore, with possible travel across our markets

- Responsibility from day one and professional and personal growth
- Private healthcare

- FPS

Market Intelligence

- Cross-border payment innovations

- Treasury partnerships
- Payment infrastructure partnerships
- Experience working in:

- Digital assets

What You'll Do

Fundraising

title: Director, Partnerships, Greater China (Singapore)
description:
About The Role

About the role

Shopify has no office in mainland China, Hong Kong, or Taiwan. This role is what we have instead.

Chinese merchants are building some of the fastest growing direct-to-consumer brands in the world, and they are building them for customers outside China. Greater China export is a top global priority, with product, infrastructure, and go-to-market investment landing behind it now. None of it reaches merchants without partners, and no partner in this market commits to a platform they have not met in person.

You are the face of Shopify partnerships in Greater China. In market, in the room, at the dinner, on the stage. You build the relationships that turn into merchants, and you find the opportunities nobody has written down yet.

You build on an ecosystem of more than a thousand active agencies, system integrators, developers, and technology partners, alongside the domestic commerce platforms that hundreds of thousands of Chinese merchants already sell on. Uniquely across Asia Pacific, technology partners here outnumber agencies, which changes what the ecosystem can do and how you build it. You own it end to end, and you are accountable for what it produces: merchants launched, merchants that survive and grow, and a partner base that gets measurably better at Shopify every quarter.

The work is genuinely unfinished. Partner capability is uneven, merchant success after launch is low, and the operating model is still being built. You will be making calls with incomplete data, in a market that moves faster than most, on one of the biggest openings Shopify has.

What you'll own



- Agency and SI partnerships across mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, including the managed partner portfolio and the team that runs it.
- Technology partnerships, including export-focused partners and the global platform relationships that matter most here.
- The import motion, currently run centrally and transitioning to you.
- Platform and joint venture relationships, including the domestic commerce platforms that are our most scalable route into the merchant long tail.
- A growing in-market team, including a Partner Solutions Engineer and a Partner Marketing Manager, both new roles.


What you'll do

Be Shopify in this market



- Be in market constantly. Partner offices, factory floors, merchant warehouses, industry events, dinners. Deals here get made in person, by people who keep showing up.
- Build a personal network at the top of the ecosystem: agency founders, platform executives, trade association leaders, and the category leaders in the export verticals that matter. Be the call they take.
- Create opportunities that are not on anyone's plan. Invent the pilot, the coalition, the program, the event. Test it with a handful of partners in weeks and scale what works.
- Move at the speed of the market. A good idea executed this month beats a better idea next quarter.
- Carry Shopify's story publicly: stage, press, WeChat, industry forums, partner communities. Be the reason a Chinese founder has heard of us.


Own the Greater China partner strategy



- Set the partner strategy for mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan: which partners we recruit, which we invest in, which we scale, and which we let go. Reason from first principles rather than the orthodox answer, and defend those calls with evidence.
- Build the partner base against where merchant demand is actually going: cross-border D2C, brand building in Western markets, and enterprise migration off local and legacy platforms.


Drive launches, merchant success, and partner capability



- Own the volume and the quality of partner-led merchant launches. Chinese agency partners already launch hundreds of stores every quarter. Far too few of those merchants go on to succeed.
- Hold partners accountable for what happens after launch, not just at it: traffic, conversion, and merchant survival. This is the number that matters most in this market.
- Own partner-sourced pipeline and the commercial relationship with the Greater China sales, solutions engineering, and marketing teams, and lift partner-led merchants into higher value plans.
- Most Chinese sellers compete on price and product rather than brand, and lack the fundamentals of Western direct-to-consumer commerce. Build the enablement model that makes partners genuinely good at teaching this, in market and in language, and take them from selling Shopify to architecting and delivering on it.
- Localize Shopify product launches and roadmap changes so partners can act on them in weeks rather than quarters.


Build a scaled motion into the long tail



- The long tail of Chinese export merchants is the largest opportunity here and the most expensive to serve directly. Design the motion that reaches it: partner-delivered, platform-delivered, and product-delivered rather than headcount-delivered.
- Own the relationships with domestic commerce platforms that can acquire and train merchants at scale on our behalf, including train-the-trainer models that use their existing sales and operations teams. Prove the unit economics before we scale, and kill what does not work.


Build and lead the team



- Lead and grow a distributed, in-market team with clear ownership, high standards, and a high pace. Onboard new roles as they land, absorb the responsibilities currently held centrally, and build the team through addition and subtraction.
- Coach the craft yourself. You will be in partner meetings, on deal reviews, and in the detail, not managing from a dashboard.
- Be the credible internal voice for Greater China with Shopify's global partnerships, product, and commercial leadership. Surface problems early, with a solution attached.


Multiply the market's impact with AI



- Merchant willingness to pay for professional services here is very low. AI is the most credible way to serve a long tail that will not pay for people, so push AI adoption into the partner ecosystem and into the tooling partners put in front of merchants.
- Use AI across your own work and your team's. Aim for what was not possible before, not marginal time savings, and own the output whether AI generated it or not.


What success looks like

Within your first six months, you will have:



- Built a named relationship map across the top agencies, technology partners, platforms, and industry bodies in the region, with you personally connected at decision-maker level across most of it.
- At least two opportunities in flight that were not on the plan when you joined, sourced from your own network and time in market.
- Published a clear Greater China partner strategy across agencies, technology partners, import, and platform relationships, with a named portfolio, explicit investment choices, and the metrics you own.
- Improved the quality of partner-led launches, with evidence that merchants launched by partners are surviving and growing, and delivered against partner-sourced pipeline targets.
- Stood up at least one scaled long-tail motion with real merchant volume and unit economics you can defend.
- Onboarded the new in-market roles, absorbed the responsibilities transitioning to you, and become the person the Greater China commercial, product, and marketing teams call when they need a door opened.


What you'll bring



- An existing, activatable network across the Greater China partner landscape: agencies and system integrators, technology partners, domestic commerce platforms, potential joint venture partners, and industry and trade associations. You should be able to open doors in your first weeks, not your first year.
- Evidence you create opportunities rather than manage them. You have built something from nothing: a market, a business, a category, a partner motion. You can point at deals that exist only because you made them exist.
- Presence and persuasion. You can hold a room, host a table of founders, and be the person they want to work with. Here the relationship comes before the contract.
- Relentless energy, and the follow-through to convert it.
- Ten or more years in partnerships, channel, alliances, or ecosystem roles with significant time in Greater China, or an unconventional path that produced the same network and the same results.
- Native Mandarin language proficiencies to liaise with clients in the Greater China Region and professional English. You can hold a technical discussion with a partner CTO in one and a commercial forecast review with global leadership in the other.
- Deep knowledge of the Chinese export ecommerce ecosystem, and enough credibility on brand building and Western direct-to-consumer fundamentals to be taken seriously by a merchant who has only ever competed on price.
- A record of owning a business outcome through partners, not just relationships, with the discipline to forecast it and hit it, and experience building a leveraged motion where reach grew faster than headcount.
- Experience leading distributed teams across markets and time zones, and comfort with ambiguity: incomplete data, evolving tooling, and a strategy being written as you go.
- Technical fluency with software platforms and integrations, enough to hold a credible conversation with a partner about what they are building.
- Demonstrated use of AI in your day-to-day craft, with examples of how it changed your scale, speed, or quality of decisions, and strong written communication. Much of your influence at Shopify is exercised in writing, to people you have never met.


Nice to have



- Experience in commerce, ecommerce, or SaaS, particularly cross-border.
- Cantonese, in addition to Mandarin and English.
- Experience standing up a partner motion in a market without a local Shopify presence.


How you work



- You would rather be in a partner's office than an internal meeting.
- You are unorthodox. You find the angle nobody else saw, and you test it before anyone gives you permission.
- You ruthlessly prioritize. Mission critical work gets resourced and everything else stops, and your team knows the difference.
- You ship weekly, not quarterly.
- You take extreme ownership. You dive deep into the details of your team's work and you own its mistakes.
- You invite challenge, including your own ideas, and you let the best idea win. You resolve conflict rather than route around it.
- You put Shopify first, ahead of the org, the team, and yourself.


How this role is structured

This is a build-phase role inside a dedicated, in-market China team. Ecosystem aim and strategy for the market is set by Shopify's VP of Product for China. You own partner strategy and execution against that aim, and you report to the Director of Partnerships for Asia Pacific.

You are the most senior Shopify partnerships leader in Greater China and you carry that externally. The title exists to open doors. Use it.

As the in-market team is staffed through the coming year, the longer term reporting structure will be confirmed. Expect to help shape it rather than inherit it. If a settled org chart is what you need to do your best work, this is not the right role.

Location and travel

Based in Singapore, working standard Greater China business hours with flexibility for teams in Singapore, Australia, and North America.

Expect to be on the road at least half your time across mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, plus occasional regional and global travel. This is not a role you can run from a desk in Singapore.

About Shopify

Opportunity is not evenly distributed. Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to over 8,300 employees and generated over $1 trillion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries.

This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option.

About You

Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means Shopify is not the right place for everyone.

Before you apply, consider if you can:



- Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone
- Excel by seeking professional and personal hypergrowth
- Keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter)
- Be resilient and resourceful in face of ambiguity and thrive on (rather than endure) change
- Bring critical thought and opinion
- Put AI agents and tools to work on the tasks they're built for, and focus on the work only humans can do
- Embrace differences and disagreement to get shit done and move forward
- Work digital-first for your daily work


We may use AI-enabled tools to screen, select, and assess applications. All AI outputs are reviewed and validated by our recruitment team.

title: Listing & Ecosystem Partnership Specialist

description:
About MEXC


Founded in 2018, MEXC is a global cryptocurrency exchange serving millions of users worldwide. We are committed to building a secure, efficient, and accessible platform for digital asset trading.


MEXC is known for offering some of the lowest trading fees in the market, deep liquidity across a wide range of assets, and fast access to trending tokens. Our platform provides a comprehensive suite of services including spot trading, derivatives, staking, and other digital asset products designed for both retail and institutional users.
Built on high-performance infrastructure and a user-first philosophy, MEXC delivers fast execution, strong market depth, and a seamless trading experience for global users.


At MEXC, we believe the best platforms are built through constant improvement and open collaboration. We value direct communication, practical thinking, and individuals who take ownership of their ideas. Teams are encouraged to share insights, challenge assumptions, and contribute to how the platform evolves.


As the digital asset industry continues to evolve, we remain focused on innovation, transparency, and global expansion while building a trusted platform for the next generation of financial technology.


Key Responsibilities



- Source and pro‑prospect high‑quality global crypto projects across key verticals including BTC‑ecosystem, Meme, AI, RWA and TradFi‑related new‑asset segments; continuously build and expand high‑quality project partner pipelines. ‑
- Conduct initial project screening and assessment against exchange listing criteria covering project fundamentals, on‑chain metrics, community health, smart‑contract audit status and market‑making commitments. Lead cross‑functional alignment with internal listing‑operations, tech, compliance, market‑making and marketing teams together with external project teams to drive smooth token listing execution. 
-  Design end‑to‑end bundled cooperation proposals for high‑potential projects, combining token listing plus Launchpad / Kickstarter / Airdrop+ campaigns, marketing initiatives and market‑making resources, to deepen project commitment and build benchmark partnership cases. 
- Coordinate market‑makers, quantitative firms, media & KOLs and ecosystem resources; support pre‑ and post‑listing delivery of liquidity, brand exposure and user‑acquisition deliverables for partner projects. 
- Track hot‑sector trends, competitor listing moves and project‑ecosystem updates; produce regular project intelligence and listing‑trend analysis to inform internal listing‑strategy decisions. 
- Maintain long‑term relationships with live‑listed project teams, monitor post‑listing business performance, and drive repeat deep‑collaboration opportunities such as secondary campaigns, contract‑product expansion and joint ecosystem building to strengthen platform reputation within the project‑builder community.


Requirements



- Minimum 5 years of professional experience within crypto / Web3 industry, with hands‑on background from crypto exchange, Web3 project‑side or ecosystem‑partnership roles; solid practical knowledge of token‑listing workflows and project due‑diligence frameworks. ‑
- Proven business communication and negotiation capabilities; capable of representing the exchange for equal‑level conversations with core project‑founder teams. Business‑level bilingual proficiency in both Chinese and English; must be comfortable conducting full‑cycle outreach and negotiations with overseas counterparties in English. 
- Existing hands‑on network of project teams, market‑making firms, KOL influencers or other Web3‑ecosystem channels is strongly preferred. 
- Result‑driven mindset, high stress tolerance, capable of managing multiple concurrent projects under fast‑paced global‑time‑zone collaborative environment. 
- Bonus qualifications: Proven end‑to‑end track record of getting projects successfully listed on top‑tier crypto exchanges; hands‑on Launchpad / asset‑issuance or ecosystem‑operation experience; deep‑rooted network within one or more focus verticals (BTC‑ecosystem, Meme, AI, RWA); previous Web3‑project‑team background with dual‑perspective understanding of both exchange‑platform and project‑builder needs.

At MEXC, we believe people do their best work when they are trusted with real responsibility and given the freedom to grow.

title: Senior Manager, Business Development - Rest of Asia (Taiwan & Hong Kong Operators / China CE Partnerships)
description:

Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

In building and scaling our business across the Rest of Asia, we've established partnerships with leading mobile, broadband, and PayTV operators in Taiwan and Hong Kong (e.g. CHT Group, Taiwan Mobile, PCCW/CSL), as well as with the largest Mainland China consumer electronics manufacturers (e.g. Hisense, TCL, Xiaomi, Oppo) that ship smart TVs and mobile devices across the region and globally.

Chinese CE OEMs in particular are now among the largest and fastest-growing players in the global TV ecosystem, making them ever more strategic partners for Netflix.

Responsibilities



- You will forge and manage commercial partnerships with mobile, broadband, and PayTV operators in Taiwan and Hong Kong, building new bundles and promotions and deepening existing relationships to streamline Netflix membership and viewing in an efficient manner.
- You will lead commercial relationships with Mainland China consumer electronics and mobile manufacturers, and provide support in structuring and commercial alignments in device placement, promotional, and distribution agreements that maximize discovery, reach, and viewing for current and prospective members.
- You will develop and execute the partnership strategy and roadmap for this territory, identifying new bundling, distribution, and promotional opportunities, and prioritizing them based on business impact.
- You will own the deal lifecycle end-to-end - from business case development and support closing out commercial alignments to be reflected through contracting and ongoing account management - and will track partner performance against agreed goals.
- You will work closely with colleagues in Partner Engagement, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Finance to translate commercial agreements into successful technical integrations and go-to-market execution.
- You will analyze market data and competitive dynamics to identify trends and opportunities, and create compelling market and business analyses for internal leadership and partner-facing conversations.
- You will represent Netflix externally with senior partner stakeholders, and internally as part of the Rest of Asia Business Development and Partnerships team.

The Ideal Candidate



-  Minimum 12 years of experience in Business Development, partnerships, or commercial roles with a technology, telecom, consumer electronics, or media company
- Experience partnering with telecom operators, PayTV/ISPs, consumer electronics manufacturers, or adjacent industries, ideally in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and/or Mainland China
- Proven track record in structuring, negotiating, and closing commercial partnership agreements
- Deep understanding of the streaming video landscape and consumer behavior in Greater China markets
- Ability to work effectively with cross-functional leaders across Product, Marketing, Legal, Finance, and Partner Engineering
- Experience drafting, negotiating, and closing term sheets and contracts
- Strong analytical and business-case skills; able to translate market data into strategy and clear recommendations
- Strong self-organization and prioritization abilities; comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy
- Fluent proficiency in Mandarin and English; Cantonese a plus

Inclusion is a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you want an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and celebrate diversity, recognizing that diversity builds stronger teams. We approach diversity and inclusion seriously and thoughtfully. title: Partner Sales Manager
description:
Your role at Dynatrace

This role is open to candidates based either in Jakarta, Indonesia or Singapore, with the successful candidate supporting their local market. Please note that we are only able to consider citizens and Permanent Residents (PR) of these respective locations, and relocation assistance is not available.

As a Partner Sales Manager, you will be responsible to recruit, develop and manage partner business in a defined geographic region focused on generating incremental, distributed software license and service-related revenue. Within the defined sales region, efforts are focused solely on Dynatrace’s Software Intelligence platform for the Enterprise Cloud.

Responsibilities also include generating interest in the Dynatrace platform by leveraging the partner ecosystem. For both regional and national partners, the objective is to develop strategic relationships through the creation of joint business initiatives and offerings that leverage Dynatrace as a fundamental component of the partner’s business. Partner Managers jointly develop sales strategies with their partners and implement those initiatives by working with local sales teams. Partner Managers are required to travel selectively to meet with partners and sales teams to gain commitment to launch an initiative and ensure successful execution of the established programs.

Responsibilities



- Understand the Partners’ business and align Dynatrace solutions to develop compelling ‘go to market’ propositions
- Qualify new Partners and demonstrate ability to effectively communicate the value of the Dynatrace platform to both C-level’ business leaders and ‘technical’ staff members
- Develop Partners to become self-sufficient in the marketing of the jointly developed solutions
- Develop and build similar sales strategies with all assigned partners in region
- Communicate in region partner activities to other Dynatrace Partner managers so they can leverage that on the jointly developed partner initiatives in their regions
- Manage, Track and Report highest priority action items, results, business plan development, marketing-related successes and accurate partner forecasts, sales
- Perform as an evangelist to drive Dynatrace solutions
- Collaborate with the region sales leadership team and successfully execute the region partner business plan
- Host quarterly business reviews with partners to drive accountability and report on success metrics
- Generate partner-sourced net-new sales pipeline and revenue

What Will Help You Succeed



- A minimum of 10 years experience in software sales, business development, channel/partner management
- A proven track record of overachievement against targets

title: Senior Manager, Business Development & Partnerships Manager
description:
Job Description

We are seeking a Business Development Manager to drive the origination and commercialisation of Keppel's future subsea cable systems. Together with the Technical Team, you will own the market intelligence that helps shape route selection, build the partnerships and consortiums that make joint builds possible, landing parties, co-investors and anchor customers that underpin each project's business case. Lead the sales of the FPs through the negotiations of IRU and O&M agreement with target customers.

This is a relationship-driven, commercially sharp role for someone who knows the global subsea ecosystem — hyperscalers, carriers, landing parties and supporting engagements with suppliers, investors and lenders.

1: Market intelligence, insights and origination



-  Own Keppel's market view of the global and regional subsea cable landscape: capacity supply and demand, route economics, pricing trends (IRU, lease and spectrum), and competitor system announcements — producing regular insight reports and demand forecasts that inform investment decisions and underwriting assumptions.
-  Track emerging trends shaping future demand — AI and hyperscale data centre growth, cloud region expansion, edge connectivity, cable resilience and route diversity requirements, and new technologies
-  Originate and qualify new system opportunities: route feasibility (with technical teams), addressable demand, competitive positioning leading to development of business case
-  Represent Keppel at key industry forums and convert conference presence into pipeline.

2: Strategic Partnerships & Customer Engagements 



-  Identify, originate and secure strategic partners, co-investors and anchor customers for new cable systems, including hyperscalers, Global Carriers, etc
-  Lead the structuring and negotiation of all commercial arrangements — from consortium and investment agreements (MOUs, JBAs, LPAs, Fibre Pair allocations, governance frameworks) through to customer contracts (IRUs, capacity and spectrum agreements, leases and O&M arrangements) — from term sheet to execution.
-  Manage all partnership relationships (together with Technical Teams) across the full lifecycle — through development, construction and into service — aligning stakeholders on route selection, system design, commercial structure, supplier strategy, budget and schedule, and capturing upgrade, renewal and expansion opportunities.
-  Assist with regulatory, licensing and market entry initiatives, including building of business cases, securing landing parties, backhaul arrangements and necessary government and industry stakeholder support.
-  Develop and execute go-to-market, pricing and commercialisation strategies for each system, ensuring alignment with investment cases, underwriting assumptions and long-term revenue objectives.
-  Identify adjacent revenue opportunities across the Keppel ecosystem — including data centre interconnection, marine services and integrated connectivity solutions — and work closely with various corporate functions and external advisers to develop bankable transaction structures.

3: Investment Case & Commercial



-  Own the investment approval papers, ensuring underwriting assumptions are robust, defensible and aligned with fund co-investor requirements.
-  Working with Keppel's Fund Management & Investment & Commercial Project manager to build the investment case and underwriting model for new subsea cable projects
-  Develop and maintain the full project financial model: capex and opex build-up, capacity sales assumptions (IRUs, leases, spectrum), revenue phasing, returns analysis (IRR, MOIC, payback) and sensitivity/scenario testing.

Join our vibrant and inclusive workforce to shape a better future for all!

Job Requirements

Required Skills:



-  10+ years' business development, sales or commercial experience in subsea cables, international wholesale telecoms, or digital infrastructure.
-  Established network across the subsea ecosystem — hyperscalers, international carriers, landing parties and/or suppliers — with a track record of originating and closing complex deals.
-  Direct experience negotiating JBA, IRU, capacity, spectrum and/or O&M agreements.
-  Strong understanding of subsea cable economics: build costs, capacity pricing, IRU structures, O&M cost allocation and consortium models.
-  Excellent research and analytical skills, with the ability to turn market data into credible demand forecasts and investment narratives.
-  Outstanding relationship-building, negotiation and presentation skills at C-level.
-  Willingness to travel extensively across multiple regions.

Preferred Skills



-  Experience forming or managing cable consortiums
-  Familiarity with landing party arrangements, cable landing licensing regimes (e.g. IMDA FBO licenses, US FCC landing licenses) and permitting in multiple jurisdictions.
-  Understanding of technical details of open cable architectures
-  Experience working alongside investment/fund management teams or with co-investment structures.
-  Degree in business, engineering, economics or a related field; regional language skills a plus.

BUSINESS SEGMENT

Connectivity

PLATFORM

Operating Division

title: Senior Manager, Strategic Partnerships
description:
About The Company

Founders today are building global companies from day one — but the systems that manage their money were built for a different era. Aspire exists to change that!

We’re building the financial operating system for global founders, bringing banking, software, and automation into a single platform so businesses can move faster across borders and stay focused on building.

Aspire is built by people who think from first principles, care deeply about solving hard problems, and take real ownership of their work. Our team brings global experience from leading fintech and technology companies, and many of us are former founders and operators who understand what it takes to build thoughtfully, make trade-offs, and deliver at scale in a global environment.

Backed by leading global investors including Y Combinator, Peak XV, and Lightspeed, Aspire has been trusted by more than 50,000 startups and growing businesses worldwide to manage their finances since 2018. Together with partners like J.P. Morgan, Visa, and Wise, we’re building for the next generation of global companies.

About The Role

Aspire is moving up-market, and partnerships is how we intend to get there. Mid-market companies — think 50 to 500 employees — don't choose their finance stack from a website. They choose it on the advice of their accountant, their ERP implementation partner, or the systems integrator who's been in their business for three years. This role builds Aspire's presence in that ecosystem across Singapore and Hong Kong.

You'll be building the partner motion, not inheriting one. That means defining the partner segments, signing the first partners in each, designing the commercial models and enablement, and standing up the co-sell motion with our direct sales team. You'll do it as an individual contributor with the full weight of the Partnerships, Sales, Marketing, and Product teams behind you — and with the expectation that what you build here becomes the template for the next market.

If you want a role where the programme already exists and your job is to run it, this isn't it. If you want to own a channel from a blank page and have the commercial results attributed to you, read on.

About The Team

Our Partnerships tribe builds and manages the relationships that extend Aspire's reach. You'll work with banks, platforms, and other partners to unlock new opportunities for our customers.

What You'll Own



- Own the partner-sourced revenue plan for mid-market across Singapore and Hong Kong, with broader APAC expansion as the motion proves out
- Identify, recruit, and sign the partners that mid-market finance teams already trust: large and mid-tier accounting firms, ERP vendors, systems integrators, ISVs, and technology consultants
- Build and manage the ERP reseller and VAR channel — partner tiering, margin and revenue-share structures, deal registration, and clear rules of engagement with direct sales
- Negotiate partnership agreements and design commercial models that hold up for both sides
- Run joint business planning and quarterly reviews with top partners: agreed targets, named pipeline, and a shared plan to deliver against it
- Build partner enablement — the collateral, training, and certification that lets a partner's own team position and sell Aspire without you in the room

What You Need To Be Successful

- Strong commercial instincts: you can structure and negotiate a revenue share, a referral fee, or a reseller margin, and you know which one fits the situation

title: Financial Partnerships Lead - Market Expansion Lead, Singapore/Hong Kong/Malaysia
categories: Software Development, Financial Services, and IT Services and IT Consulting
description:
About the Xendit
Xendit is an enterprise payments platform powering complex financial operations across Southeast Asia and global markets. We provide a unified API layer combining payment processing, global payouts, localized FX, identity compliance, and fraud protection. As a trusted financial partner backed by top-tier global investors, Xendit processes high-throughput transaction flows for leading global platforms including Meta, Traveloka, ByteDance, Wise, and Grab, building resilient payment infrastructure to drive regional commerce forward


About the Job
Xendit is going from a Southeast Asian payments provider to a global one. Nothing in that sentence happens without rails. Every market we want to sell in has to exist before it can be sold in — an entity, a licence or a licensed partner, bank accounts, and live rails — and every market we already sell in only earns what its partner economics allow


This role owns both halves, at roughly equal weight


Market expansion. You will help decide which markets we enter, build the case that gets them funded, choose whether we build, buy, or partner for the licence, and then run the entry end to end until the market is licensed, funded, connected, and handed over to a country commercial lead. You will do it as a repeatable playbook rather than a one-off project, so the second market is faster than the first and the fifth is faster than the second


Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong. You will own Xendit’s financial partner portfolio in those three markets — the banks, wallets, card schemes, FX providers and domestic rails we run on. You own the relationships, the commercials, the performance, and the cost of every rail in your markets


Responsibilities


Market expansion

- Market intelligence. Screen and rank candidate markets on market size, regulatory openness, payment rails, competitive density, and merchant demand. Maintain a live pipeline and a decision-ready entry book per market
- Business case and investment decision. Build the cost-to-launch and cost-to-operate model, the revenue and margin projection, and the breakeven view. Take the go/no-go paper to leadership and defend it
- Licensing strategy. Recommend build, buy, or partner per market. Select the licence type, shape the regulator engagement approach, and hold a coherent licensing roadmap across markets rather than a footprint we did not design
- Foundational set-up. Drive entity incorporation, the licence application end to end, bank account opening, and scheme and rail access — executing with Corporate Secretarial, Legal, Compliance, and Treasury
- Programme management. One timeline, one budget, one risk register per market. Convene the functions, hold them to dates, and escalate early and specifically when a gate is at risk
- The playbook. Turn each entry into reusable artefacts — stage gates, application pack templates, a common business case model, a bank account approach, a handover checklist — and own the country-specific deviations
- Handover. Support the hire of the country commercial lead, operationalise the licence with Compliance, and hand over against a defined readiness bar. Until every item on that bar is true, the market is still yours


Financial partnerships in Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong

- Partner portfolio strategy. Decide which partners we run which rails and corridors on, where we need redundancy, and what the partner roadmap is for each of the three markets
- Commercials. Negotiate pricing, rebates, revenue share, and FX spreads. Use volume across markets as leverage rather than negotiating each market from scratch. Own the contract lifecycle with Legal
- Cost of rails. Own COGS in your markets. Find the margin, model it, and work with Product and Treasury to move routing and volume to where the economics are better
- Partner performance. Set and enforce SLAs, run QBRs, chase root causes when a rail underperforms, and manage escalations with the partner rather than around them
- Regulatory posture with partners. Keep partner flows appropriate to our licences in each market, make sure agreements carry the right AML and KYC responsibilities, and give Compliance and the country teams a clear view of each partner’s regulatory role
- Being the accountable owner. Every partnership has one accountable owner. For these markets, it is you. Other teams can talk to partners directly for execution and compliance; nothing material happens without you
- Unblocking commercial deals. Support sales cycles that turn on a partner capability we do not yet have, and bring the market and merchant insight back into the global partner strategy


The Questions You Will Answer

- Which markets should Xendit enter next, in what order, and which ones should we decline?
- What will it actually cost and how long will it actually take to be able to process a first transaction there?
- Do we build our own licence, acquire one, or launch on a partner’s — and what does that trade in cost, speed, control, and margin?
- What has to be true before we commit commercially or hire in a market?
- Where is the margin in Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong, and what has to change to get it?
- Which rails in these markets are a single point of failure, and what is the backup?
- What did the last entry teach us that makes the next one cheaper and faster?
- Is this market genuinely ready to run itself, or are we handing over a problem?


Minimum Qualifications

- 3+ years of experience running a complex cross-functional programme to a committed date — not only designing the plan, but landing it. Backgrounds that travel well here include top-tier management consulting, corporate development or strategy at a high-growth technology or financial services company, and programme leadership at a payments, banking, or fintech business
- Experience running a complex cross-functional programme to a committed date — not only designing the plan, but landing it. Backgrounds that travel well here include top-tier management consulting, corporate development or strategy at a high-growth technology or financial services company, and partnership or programme leadership at a payments, banking, or fintech business
- A track record of negotiating and running commercial relationships with banks, card schemes, wallets, or payment providers. You have held a number and moved it
- Working knowledge of payment regulation, banking, and payment infrastructure. You do not need to be a lawyer. You do need to hold a credible conversation with a regulator, a global bank, and our own Compliance team on the same day
- Strong commercial and financial judgment: you can build the model, stress the assumptions, and say plainly when a market does not clear the bar
- Exceptional written communication. Much of the output of this role is a paper that a CEO, a board, or a regulator reads without you in the room
- A genuine global operator who translates across cultures and domains. Relationship building and regulator engagement in developed markets do not work the way they do in Southeast Asia, and this role has to work in both. Familiarity with the Malaysian, Singaporean, or Hong Kong payments landscape is a clear advantage
- A strong team player. On the expansion half this role has no line authority over the functions it depends on and has to earn its way through them
- Comfort with ambiguity and with owning an outcome that is largely dependent on other people’s work
- A bachelor’s degree in an analytically rigorous discipline


You Will Thrive Here If You

- Are more interested in the market going live than in the plan being elegant
- Sequence properly: you establish whether we can be licensed, at what cost and by when, before anyone commits
- Bring functions in at the start as inputs rather than at the end as approvers, and hold them to dates without turning it into a fight
- Are willing to recommend a no-go on a market leadership is excited about, with the analysis to support it
- Build things that outlast you: templates, models, and playbooks the next person inherits.
- Are energised by a fast pace, high accountability, and direct feedback


Working Model

- Based in Singapore or Hong Kong
- We expect team members in the office four days per week to support close collaboration and fast decisions
- Travel of approximately 20–30%, to target markets, regulators, banks, and partners, weighted to the entries in flight


Why This Role?

- Most people who work on market entry do one market, once, inside a function. Here you own the whole sequence — the screen, the case, the licence, the accounts, the rails, the handover — and then you own it again in the next market, with the advantage of having built the playbook. It is one of the few roles where the scope of what you own is genuinely limited only by how fast you can make the machine work
- If you want a defined lane inside an established process, this is not the role. If you want to build the capability that decides where a payments company can operate, we would like to hear from you

Across its platforms, Trip.com Group integrates travel resources from industry partners and helps travellers worldwide pursue the perfect trip with exceptional travel products and services.

corporations and more than 980,000 small and medium-sized enterprises globally. Our global customer

In this Role, you’ll get to

title: Partnerships Manager APAC
description:
Company Description

Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.

Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.

Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money.

For everyone, everywhere.

Job Description

More about our mission and what we offer.

We are looking for an ambitious and commercially minded Partnerships Manager to join our Strategic Partnerships team in Singapore. You will play a critical role in helping Wise accelerate growth across APAC by building and scaling partnerships that connect us with customers who have international money needs.

APAC is one of Wise's fastest-growing regions and a key growth opportunity. Across international students, travellers, expats and other globally-minded communities, we see significant potential to reach more customers through strategic partnerships.

This is a new role within a global team with high autonomy to own the end to end regional strategy. Working closely with regional growth teams, you will identify, negotiate and launch partnerships across APAC, adapting global opportunities to local markets and turning them into measurable growth.

The goal will be to use your commercial talents to unlock new groups of customers who have a need for Wise, but didn't know enough about us to use us before.

This is not a Wise Platform role - Your main goal is to accelerate personal adoption of Wise in APAC markets.

Responsibilities



- Strategy & Planning

- Define and execute the APAC partnership strategy across consumer partnerships, focused on helping internationally-minded customers discover and use Wise.
- Own, optimise and grow partnership verticals with full autonomy in collaboration with the global team
- Identify and prioritise high-intent customer segments with recurring international money needs, including international students, working holiday travellers, group travel communities, relocation and migration customers
- Build market-level partnership plans that align with regional growth priorities and business objectives
- Forecast partnership impact and prioritise opportunities based on customer acquisition, volume and long-term value
- Sourcing & Negotiation & Execution 

- Prospect, qualify and develop relationships with potential partners across Australia, Singapore, Malaysia and broader APAC markets
- Own the full partnership lifecycle from outreach and discovery through to negotiation, contracting, launch and optimisation
- Structure commercial agreements that create value for both Wise and our partners
- Build scalable partnership frameworks that can be replicated across markets and partner categories.
- Go-To-Market & Execution

- Oversee the end-to-end launch of partnership campaigns, working closely with brand, regional growth, legal and product teams to ensure smooth delivery
- Performance & Optimisation

- Define and track key performance indicators for each partnership, including metrics across the funnel that drive measurable growth
- Use data to identify performance trends, opportunities and challenges, turning insights into actions that improve results.
- Maintain and nurture long-term relationships with existing partners, identifying opportunities for expansion, renewal, and increased investment based on proven results
- Regional Collaboration

- Act as the local partnerships expert within APAC
- Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders across regional marketing, growth, product and strategy teams
- Share market insights and partnership learnings that help shape future regional and global initiatives
Qualifications

A Bit About You



- Proven Partnership Success: You have experience sourcing, negotiating and executing successful partnerships that deliver measurable commercial outcomes. Experience working across APAC markets is a strong advantage. You can demonstrate how your work has driven customer acquisition, revenue growth, engagement or other business-critical metrics.
- Commercial Acumen: You are a natural at structuring and closing diverse commercial deals, big or small. You know how to identify opportunities, evaluate potential impact and make sound investment decisions.
- Strategic Yet Hands-On: You enjoy thinking strategically but are equally comfortable rolling up your sleeves and executing. You can take an idea from concept through to launch and optimisation.
- Strong Relationship Builder: You are naturally skilled at building trust with both external partners and internal stakeholders. You understand how to navigate different cultures, communication styles and business environments.
- Strong Analytical Mindset: You love diving into data, spotting trends, and unearthing insights that directly shape winning strategies and forecasts
- Culturally Adaptable: You are comfortable building relationships across different countries, cultures and business environments. You understand how to adapt your approach to local markets while maintaining a consistent commercial strategy.
- Self-Starter: You thrive in ambiguity, enjoy solving problems and are motivated by the opportunity to build and scale something new in a fast-growing region.
- Results-Oriented: You are focused on outcomes and have a track record of delivering against ambitious commercial targets while managing multiple priorities.
- AI-Curious: You actively explore emerging technologies and find innovative ways to integrate AI into your workflows, continuously seeking to improve efficiency and scale your impact.
- Mission-Driven: You are deeply aligned with our core purpose and bring an intrinsic motivation to your work, ensuring that your daily contributions directly advance our long-term vision.

Nice-to-have 



- Experience in FinTech, Payments or Financial Services
- Experience in travel, student, migration, relocation or international consumer businesses
- Experience using AI and analytical tools
- Fluency in an Asian language
- Experience working in high-growth technology companies

Additional Information

What’s in it for you?

This will be an opportunity to define and drive how Wise does strategic partnerships. There are no limitations to who we can work with (where the commercial opportunity is robustly justified). You will develop skills in many different verticals all at once and be given resources to do it quickly.

You’ll have the chance to work in a friendly and supportive atmosphere with plenty of opportunities to grow and be part of our revolution. This includes a company funded personal development budget to spend on training, books and events.

Want to find out more about the team? Find out more about what Partnerships means at Wise here and what life is like in the team here.

We’re people without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too.

We want to work with the best people, no matter their background. So if you’re passionate about learning new things and keen to join our mission, you’ll fit right in.

Also, where and what you studied isn’t important to us. If you’ve got great experience, the right skills for the role and you’re great at articulating your thinking, we’d like to hear from you.

If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.

Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.

We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.

Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.

If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.

Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

title: Sr. Partner Development Manager

To learn more about life at LogicMonitor, check out our Careers Page.

What You'll Do:

LogicMonitor® is the AI-first hybrid observability platform powering the next generation of digital infrastructure. LogicMonitor delivers complete visibility and actionable intelligence across on-premises, cloud, and edge environments. By anticipating issues before they strike, optimizing resources in real time, and enabling faster, smarter decisions, LogicMonitor helps IT and business leaders protect margins, accelerate innovation, and deliver exceptional digital experiences without compromise.

Our customers love LogicMonitor's ability to bring cloud and traditional IT together into one view, as seen in minimal churn rates, expansion business, and exciting new customer references. In fact, LogicMonitor has received the highest Net Promoter Score of any IT Infrastructure Management provider. LogicMonitor also boasts high employee satisfaction. We have been certified as a Great Place To Work®, and named one of BuiltIn's Best Places to Work for the seventh year in a row!

The mission of the Sr. Partner Development Manager, MSP is to drive new annual recurring revenue (ARR) growth and strategic partner expansion within LogicMonitor's Managed Service Provider ecosystem.

This role is responsible for identifying, engaging, and growing MSP partners by owning the full sales lifecycle—from prospecting and qualification through expansion, renewal, and long-term account development. The Partner Development Manager serves as a trusted advisor to MSP leadership teams, helping partners leverage LogicMonitor to improve operational efficiency, scale service delivery, and drive profitable growth.

Operating within a targeted account and territory model, the Partner Development Manager develops executive relationships, uncovers business challenges, and aligns LogicMonitor's observability platform to partner business objectives.

Here's a closer look at this key role:





- MSP Partner Acquisition & Pipeline Development

- Build and maintain a qualified sales pipeline of 3–5x annual quota through outbound prospecting, partner referrals, marketing-generated opportunities, industry networking, and strategic account planning.
- Build and execute a territory plan focused on identifying and engaging high-potential MSP partners.
- Generate pipeline through outbound prospecting, partner referrals, marketing-generated opportunities, and industry networking.
- Conduct discovery conversations to understand MSP business models, operational challenges, growth initiatives, and technology priorities.
- Qualify opportunities and advance them through the sales process using established sales methodologies.
- Consistently achieve pipeline generation targets, opportunity creation goals, and revenue objectives.
- Generate a significant portion of pipeline through self-sourced prospecting and account development activities.
Strategic Selling & Revenue Growth



- Own the full sales cycle from initial engagement through contract execution.
- Develop and manage opportunities across acquisition, expansion, and renewal motions.
- Collaborate with Sales Engineering to deliver demonstrations, technical evaluations, and solution workshops.
- Build business cases and articulate measurable business outcomes to both technical and executive stakeholders.
- Lead commercial discussions, negotiate contracts, and successfully close new business opportunities.
- Maintain accurate forecasting, opportunity management, and CRM hygiene.
- Consistently achieve or exceed assigned ARR and revenue targets.

Partner Relationship Management



- Establish trusted advisor relationships with MSP executives, operational leaders, and technical stakeholders.
- Develop a deep understanding of partner business objectives, service offerings, and growth strategies.
- Identify opportunities to expand LogicMonitor adoption across partner organizations and customer environments.
- Conduct regular business reviews and strategic planning sessions with key partners.
- Monitor partner health, engagement, and growth opportunities while proactively addressing risks.

Partner Enablement & Adoption



- Support partner onboarding, enablement, and ongoing adoption initiatives.

title: Strategic Partner Manager, Global Partnerships, Vietnam
description:
Meta is looking for a strategic, results-driven and people-driven Strategic Partner Manager (SPM) for the global partnerships team covering Vietnam. We are looking for someone who can own the Vietnam market end-to-end championing strategy and growth for our creator, public figure, production house, and media partners across the Family of Apps products, tools, and services.This role manages the full Vietnam partner ecosystem — public figures, creators, and production houses — and is responsible for driving product adoption and leading the end-to-end go-to-market (GTM) strategy and programs in the market. - Be the strategic advisor to the partner's business growth across Meta Family of App (FB, IG, Threads, Edits, and Meta AI)
- Identify and translate market opportunities and challenges into a well-defined strategy that drives product adoption and leads end-to-end GTM strategy and programs for the Vietnam market
- Drive goals and develop digital talent through strategic partnerships and development plans
- Build strategic collaborations with cross-functional teams, achieve shared objectives, and track key performance metrics
- Plan and execute impactful events and activations that engage partners
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to influence partner product and program development efforts both short-term feature requests and long-term strategic roadmap
- Represent Meta in external meetings with partners and present Meta's value proposition to C-suite executives

Minimum Qualifications:



- Professional fluency in Vietnamese required to manage partner relationships and communications in the Vietnam market. Business fluency in English required to collaborate with internal cross-functional teams and regional stakeholders
- 8+ years of experience in partnerships, product or go-to-market roles
- Deep knowledge of creators, public figures, production houses, and media and their ecosystem in Vietnam, preferably with an existing network of relationships with creators and emerging and/or established talents
- Experience with new business and partner development, building long-term partnerships, and partner management in Vietnam
- Managing projects independently, with the ability to lead multiple time-sensitive, cross-functional projects on deadline
- Strong communication and presentation skills, and the ability to serve as a spokesperson for Meta
- Excellent organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and influencing skills
- Demonstrated excellence in collaboration and relationship-building with internal and external stakeholders
- Familiarity with a high degree of autonomy, displaying leadership, organizational, and execution skills
- Rapid learner who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and can pivot as necessary

Preferred Qualifications:



- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field
- Preferably has experience in creator/talent management, media, label, technology, and/or gaming
- Professional fluency in Vietnamese with an excellent command of English, required for communicating with external stakeholders in the APAC region
- Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
- Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
- Experience driving growth through technology and product integrations is a major plus. Experience applying business acumen to develop and scale strategic partnerships
- Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. People who choose to build their careers by building with us at Meta help shape a future that will take us beyond what digital connection makes possible today—beyond the constraints of screens, the limits of distance, and even the rules of physics.

description:
